item.title: Sat Nov 7, 2026 — Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff, and pressure on Hegseth keeps building
item.description: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff, and pressure on Hegseth keeps building · Blowout jobs report: 165K added, unemployment falls to 4.1%, and Fed hike odds jump · Iran: U.S. hits Qeshm air defenses again as Trump claims "a lot of progress" in talks · Still counting: Colom's Mississippi lead grows to ~2,500, Peltola up 637 in Alaska, Boebert trailing
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff, and pressure on Hegseth keeps building

Facts

  • Trump said Friday that Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller will become White House chief of staff on Monday, Nov. 9. Susie Wiles, who ran his 2024 campaign and has held the job since day one of the second term, resigned Thursday night and moves to the "Trump Political Operation." It's the biggest staff change since Tuesday's midterm losses.
  • Miller designed the administration's immigration-enforcement and deportation program and has a broad policy portfolio. CNN reports Trump has been furious about the midterm results.
  • Reuters, as cited by Fox News, reports that Miller, OMB Director Russ Vought and White House lawyers have spent months listing actions Trump can take without Congress, covering immigration, tariffs, housing and spending. Trump has called himself "Mr. Veto."
  • Defense Secretary Hegseth is under growing pressure. CBS reports Trump has asked advisers whether Hegseth should stay, though Trump says publicly he's "doing a very good job." Rep. Thomas Massie plans to force a House impeachment vote as soon as next week unless Hegseth resigns. Sen. Thom Tillis has urged Trump to fire him, and Oversight Chair James Comer says there are "a lot of questions." The Pentagon says Hegseth "will not back down."

Left view

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called Miller a "dangerous xenophobe" and told Trump to fire him (The Hill). CBS News and CNN framed the promotion as Trump doubling down on the agenda voters just rejected rather than moving toward the center. Incoming Oversight Chair Robert Garcia is already planning investigations into Trump family business dealings.

Right view

Fox News presents the move as a tactical shift toward governing by executive action. One administration official called Miller "a great pick" and said reversing mass migration is the defining issue, and Kayleigh McEnany praised Miller on Fox as a "fighter." Fox also found unease among Hill Republicans. One House Republican said they'd been worried about this for two years, and another expects the White House to keep governing "without Congress."

Watch for

Expect more executive orders and vetoes, and Democratic subpoenas once the new Congress is seated in January. Whether Hegseth survives the Massie vote is the next test of how far GOP lawmakers will break with Trump. The Dec. 11 funding deadline is the first big lame-duck fight. Tariffs are on the reported list of executive actions, so don't expect trade policy to soften.

Sources: CBS News Fox News CNN Axios The Hill CBS (Hegseth) Yahoo News

Blowout jobs report: 165K added, unemployment falls to 4.1%, and Fed hike odds jump

Facts

  • The economy added 165,000 jobs in October. The Wall Street Journal's survey of economists expected about 65,000. Revisions added 84,000 to August and September, so hiring has averaged 137K a month over the last three months, up from 28K over May–July.
  • Unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. Professional services, health care, transportation and manufacturing accounted for about 94% of the gains, while leisure and hospitality lost jobs.
  • Wages rose 3.1% from a year earlier, the slowest pace since 2021 and below 3.6% PCE inflation, so real pay is still falling.
  • Fed-funds futures now put the odds of a December 8–9 rate hike at about 79%, up from about 67% Thursday (Hubbard-O'Brien Economics). The 10-year yield rose to about 4.86%.

Left view

NPR and NBC News called the report a welcome bright spot, but NBC stressed that the economy still risks stagnation. Center-left economists point out that paychecks are trailing prices, which fits voters' "affordability" anger on Tuesday. Bloomberg Intelligence's Ira Jersey noted underemployment ticked up.

Right view

The White House called it a "blowout" that "smashes expectations" and credited tariffs, tax cuts and reshoring. Fox Business and conservative economists such as Steve Moore and E.J. Antoni echoed that message. The administration is using the report to argue the midterm losses weren't about the economy.

Watch for

A December hike is now the base case for markets. That would mean higher mortgage and credit-card rates and probably a stronger dollar. The October CPI report is the next big data point. Allianz Trade's Dan North called the labor market "stable but perhaps unexciting," and the household survey still shows job losses for the year, so some economists aren't convinced.

Sources: CNBC NPR NBC News Hubbard-O'Brien White House Yahoo Finance

Iran: U.S. hits Qeshm air defenses again as Trump claims "a lot of progress" in talks

Facts

  • U.S. forces carried out limited strikes on Iranian air-defense systems on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz Friday night. Trump called it a "minor" action and said "we are not fighting." Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it shot down a U.S. drone, which the U.S. hasn't confirmed (Euronews).
  • Trump also said the U.S. has made "a lot of progress" and that Iran wants a deal. Qatar, the main mediator, denied reports that talks had collapsed.
  • Tehran says it won't discuss its nuclear program until seven conditions are met. They include ending the port blockade, lifting sanctions, unfreezing assets, paying war reparations and stopping Israeli operations in Lebanon. Security official Mohsen Rezaei, who met Putin in Moscow, says Hormuz stays shut until then (The National, Reuters). Separately, Iran's navy reported another ship fire in Hormuz.
  • Trump met his security team twice this week. Fox News reports CENTCOM is finishing preparations for a possible larger operation, but no order has been given.

Left view

Progressive outlets and Democrats call the new strikes proof that the war is still going despite Tuesday's verdict. They want Congress to enforce the War Powers Resolution, which is also the basis of Massie's Hegseth impeachment articles. International coverage (Euronews, The National) treats Iran's conditions as a sign Tehran thinks the midterms gave it leverage.

Right view

Fox News coverage highlights military readiness and the blockade as leverage, and treats limited strikes as pressure that keeps Iran negotiating. Hawks want no sanctions relief before nuclear concessions. The Vance-aligned restraint wing sees Trump's "progress" talk as a step toward the deal it has been pushing.

Watch for

The new moon on Nov. 9 favors night operations, and the USS Roosevelt arrives mid-November. Brent sits just under $100. Analysts cited this week say a big escalation would push it back above $110, while a framework deal could send it much lower and keep gas prices falling.

Sources: Euronews The National L'Orient Today Times of Israel LaPresse

Still counting: Colom's Mississippi lead grows to ~2,500, Peltola up 637 in Alaska, Boebert trailing

Facts

  • Mississippi Senate: Democrat Scott Colom's lead over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith grew from 1,813 Friday morning to 2,010 at midday and then 2,493, as he won about 70% of newly counted ballots. Officials estimate 12,000–20,000 affidavit ballots remain. Voters have until Nov. 10 to cure ballots, and counties must certify by Nov. 13.
  • Alaska Senate: Democrat Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan by 637 votes out of more than 200,000. The next mail batches arrive Monday and Tuesday. A New York Times analysis expects her lead to grow, including under ranked-choice tabulation.
  • The count so far: Democrats hold 54 Senate seats to 44 with two races outstanding. In the House they lead 253–162 with 20 uncalled, their biggest majority since 2008. Rep. Lauren Boebert (CO-4) trails Democrat Eileen Laubacher by more than 3,000 votes.
  • Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) left the hospital after a stroke. He's expected to fully recover but will miss several weeks of votes.

Left view

Democracy Docket and Mississippi Free Press report that Colom is overperforming among affidavit ballots, even in counties that favor Hyde-Smith. They call the GOP demand to "segregate and preserve" provisional ballots a setup for disqualifying voters. Colom also blames Secretary of State Michael Watson's voter-roll purge, which used Experian data, for creating many of the affidavit ballots.

Right view

State GOP chair Mike Hurst says the party will go through results county by county and act quickly if laws aren't followed. Magnolia Tribune notes the estimates of outstanding ballots aren't confirmed. Former Maricopa County recorder Stephen Richer, a Republican, said most affidavit ballots will likely count under state law.

Watch for

Mississippi has no recount law, so a close loss leads to a "ballot box exam" and then court. Wins in both outstanding races would give Democrats 56 seats, which gives them a bigger cushion on nominations and oversight next year.

Sources: Democracy Docket Mississippi Free Press Magnolia Tribune NBC News Yahoo News live

Israel: Herzog holds off on a mandate until Sunday despite Eisenkot's 67–46 edge

Facts

  • After consultations, 67 Knesset members recommended Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot and 46 backed Netanyahu. United Torah Judaism recommended no one.
  • President Herzog said the numbers look clear "on the surface," but he wants to confirm a government can actually be formed, given vetoes between and within the blocs. He's holding direct talks with party leaders and will announce Sunday, Nov. 8 (Ynet).
  • Eisenkot's support includes the Arab parties Ra'am and the Joint List alongside Yisrael Beytenu and the center-left. Yashar wants a "national emergency government" formed quickly.

Left view

Center-left Israeli and international outlets (Ynet, Al-Monitor) see Herzog's caution as procedure, not a reversal, and treat Netanyahu's exit as likely. They also question whether a coalition this broad can hold together.

Right view

Likud's Yoav Kisch warned Herzog against a government that relies on Arab parties, and pointed to Iran and Palestinian statehood as the stakes. Right-leaning Brussels Signal framed the delay as Herzog "holding back" a mandate despite a clear majority. U.S. right-leaning coverage is thin, with attention on the midterms.

Watch for

Whoever gets the mandate has 28 days, plus a possible 14-day extension. An Eisenkot government would come in as Washington decides between a deal and more strikes on Iran, and Vance is already calling for a change in U.S.–Israel ties.

Sources: Ynet Arutz Sheva France 24 Brussels Signal Al-Monitor

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,376.86 (+0.31%) Friday, −2.7% for the week, its worst since June. Dow: 51,285.73 (−237, −0.46%), −0.9% on the week. Nasdaq: 24,579.42 (+1.09%), −3.4% on the week. Chips bounced after Thursday's AI rout: AMD +10.8%, Nvidia +3.9%, with Micron and Intel also higher.
  • Oil: WTI (Dec.) settled at about $90.34, little changed. Brent is just under $100. Iran headlines (new Qeshm strikes alongside "progress" talk) keep it volatile, and energy stocks (XLE) fell about 11% for the week.
  • Gas: The AAA national average is $4.04 today, down from $4.10 Thursday and about 12¢ lower over the past week, but still more than $1 above a year ago.
  • Other: The 10-yr yield is ~4.86% after the jobs beat. Gold fell to ~$4,080 (−0.8%) and bitcoin is ~$75.8K. Airbnb beat on earnings and revenue, and Iren jumped as much as 20% on $200M in AI-cloud revenue despite a $263M loss.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Ben James shot 64 and leads the World Wide Technology Championship in Los Cabos at −15. Peter Malnati is one back after his own 64, and Zac Blair is three back. First-round leader Chris Kirk, who's fighting to keep his card, is in the pack around −9.
  • Tennis: Alcaraz saved two match points to beat Taylor Fritz 6-7(10) 7-5 6-3 in the Paris quarters, which ended Fritz's ATP Finals hopes. Saturday's semis are Alcaraz vs. Ruud and Shelton vs. Luca Van Assche. The Turin field is set: Alcaraz, Zverev, Shelton, Medvedev, Cobolli, Fils, Tiafoe and 20-year-old Rafael Jódar. The WTA Finals start today.
  • Squash: In the U.S. Open semis in Philadelphia, Diego Elias beat top seed Mostafa Asal 3-0 and Paul Coll came back from two games down to beat Aly Abou Eleinen. On the women's side, Amina Orfi edged Nour ElSherbini in five and Nouran Gohar beat Hania El Hammamy in a five-game thriller that included a 23-21 game. Finals are today: Elias vs. Coll and Orfi vs. Gohar.
  • WWE: Crown Jewel is today in Riyadh. On the go-home SmackDown, Kevin Owens beat CM Punk in a No Holds Barred main event, and Sami Zayn walked away from Jimmy Uso after a masked group ambushed Uso. The Crown Jewel card includes Reigns vs. Zayn, Chelsea Green vs. Liv Morgan for the Women's title, and Cody vs. Orton in a Last Man Standing match.
  • Hockey: Sabres 5, Blue Jackets 2, with two goals from Josh Norris and three assists from Owen Power. Wild 4, Sharks 1, with a goal and three assists from Kirill Kaprizov.
  • Soccer: Everton 3, Coventry 1 on Friday. Thierno Barry scored twice in five minutes, and Everton moved up to 5th. Frank Lampard criticized three refereeing decisions that went against Coventry. The full Premier League slate follows this weekend.
  • Football: College GameDay is in South Bend for Miami at Notre Dame. In the NFL, Week 10 is Sunday after the Jaguars' 33-10 TNF win over Baltimore. The Ravens (4-5) have lost four straight.

Trump says he "may have to" destroy the rest of the country as Qatar carries Tehran's offer · GOP blame game: Vance says "the war" cost the midterms, Trump half-agrees, and others point to tariffs · Mississippi Senate: Colom leads Hyde-Smith by ~1,100 votes, thousands of ballots to go, and there's no recount law
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

AI rout: Nasdaq −5.5% into a correction as investors bet the blue wave slows the data-center boom

Facts

  • Thursday was Wall Street's worst day since 2025. The S&P 500 fell 4.36%, the Nasdaq 5.52% (now more than 10% off its October record), and the Dow 1,835 points (−3.44%) to 51,521. That wiped out Wednesday's post-midterm rally. The VIX jumped about 60% to near 27.
  • Chips led the selloff. Micron and AMD each fell about 17%, Marvell 16% and Nvidia 9%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had its worst day since April 2025. Roughly $2–2.5 trillion in market value was erased.
  • The trigger was a Democratic push to curb data centers. Bernie Sanders called for a national moratorium, and Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa promised a pause on new approvals. Local ballot measures restricting data centers passed almost everywhere they appeared (The Guardian counted ~40 jurisdictions in 10 states). UBS estimated about 30% of planned 2028 data-center capacity is at risk.
  • The selloff spread overnight: Japan's Nikkei fell ~6% into a bear market and Korea's Kospi dropped more than 6%. U.S. futures are mixed this morning, with Nasdaq-100 up ~1.4% and the Dow down ~0.9%.

Left view

Progressives and outlets such as The Guardian read the ballot results as a voter revolt over power bills, water use and Big Tech's influence on local zoning. Democrats including Sanders, Reps. Ansari and Casar, and Ohio Senator-elect Sherrod Brown treat curbing the buildout as a mandate, not a market risk. NPR framed the rout as fear of an "AI crackdown" rather than a verdict on the economy.

Right view

Trump blamed the "Dumocrats" on Truth Social and told voters they had only themselves to blame for the "crash." Fox Business and the Washington Examiner led with his comments. The Examiner's own reporting, though, put the drop down to AI stocks rather than the election itself. Conservative commentators argue moratoriums would hand AI leadership to China and push up energy costs in other ways.

Watch for

The October jobs report lands at 8:30 ET, with consensus at roughly 55–65K jobs and 4.2% unemployment. A weak number could deepen the slide. Quilter's Stuart Clark pointed to how concentrated the market is in a handful of tech names, which makes swings like this more likely. Bloomberg reports some strategists see the backlash as making an outright AI investment bust less likely, because it slows overbuilding. Fed-hike odds for December fell from ~83% to ~70%.

Sources: StockTitan Bloomberg Washington Post NPR Business Standard Washington Examiner Yahoo Finance

Iran: strike or deal? Trump says he "may have to" destroy the rest of the country as Qatar carries Tehran's offer

Facts

  • Trump met his national security team Wednesday and Thursday. He said he'd rather not "destroy the rest of the country" but might have to, and that a decision is coming soon.
  • Axios reports CENTCOM is finishing preparations for a possible return to major operations but has no new order. Officials note a new moon on Nov. 9, which favors night operations. The U.S. blockade of Iranian ports continues.
  • Iran sent a formal nuclear proposal through Qatar (Reuters), and U.S. officials are reviewing it. Tehran's conditions include sanctions relief, an end to the blockade, release of frozen funds and a permanent end to hostilities.
  • Advisers are split: Vance favors a deal, while CIA Director Ratcliffe and Treasury Secretary Bessent reportedly want to keep the blockade. Trump brushed off reports that he'd replace Defense Secretary Hegseth. Two tankers and a tug caught fire in Hormuz, and UKMTO logged five attacks on ships since Sunday.

Left view

NPR has reported for weeks that the U.S. and Israel were planning a possible post-midterm strike, and left-leaning columnists (e.g., the Philadelphia Inquirer) warn of a deeper "misconceived" war right after voters punished it. Iranian officials, quoted widely, say the midterms show Americans rejected the war.

Right view

Fox News coverage centers on Trump's leverage, the blockade and Iran's "spiraling" economy, and treats renewed strikes as a credible way to force concessions. Trump says he is "totally convinced" the war was right to keep Iran from a bomb. The Vance-wing populists counter that the war cost the GOP the election and want a deal now.

Watch for

Oil is the tell. Brent fell below $100 on deal hopes, dropping ~8% Wednesday, then bounced back near $98. The G7 and IEA are coordinating stock releases. The USS Roosevelt carrier group won't arrive until mid-November, which some analysts read as a window for talks. A strike would likely push crude back above $110 and erase the recent relief at the pump.

Sources: Fox News Reuters Gulf News NPR Inquirer Anadolu

GOP blame game: Vance says "the war" cost the midterms, Trump half-agrees, and others point to tariffs

Facts

  • In a long post Wednesday, VP Vance blamed the Iran war for the losses. He laid out four priorities: ending the war, cutting living costs, America First, and changing the U.S. relationship with Israel.
  • Trump called Vance's read "largely true" because the war pushed up gas prices short-term, but said he'd do it again. He also said Republicans would have won if he had been on the ballot.
  • Sen. Ted Cruz, who will be Texas's only GOP senator after James Talarico beat Ken Paxton, blamed costs, tariffs and a war that's "dragged on too long." Former Sen. Pat Toomey said Vance's explanation leaves out tariffs. DeSantis called the result close to an "extinction-level event."
  • Jim Jordan and Steve Scalise are running for House minority leader. Harmeet Dhillon resigned as head of DOJ's Civil Rights Division, the first senior departure since the vote.

Left view

Democrats and liberal outlets say the war, tariffs and $4 gas are all Trump's decisions, so splitting the blame is a dodge. Rep. Jamie Raskin, in line for Judiciary chair, is already promising oversight of ICE and CBP.

Right view

Fox News describes a "reckoning." Restrainers (Vance, the Tucker Carlson wing) see vindication, while hawks reject the war-as-culprit story. Israel's UN ambassador publicly disputed Vance, as reported by Middle East Eye. Free-market conservatives like Toomey put the blame on tariffs.

Watch for

Strategists see the Vance–Trump split as an early 2028 fault line. The near-term test is whether Trump's Iran decision follows Vance's advice or the hawks'. House Democrats vote on leadership Nov. 18, and the Dec. 11 funding deadline is the first lame-duck showdown.

Sources: Fox News ABC News NewsNation Middle East Eye Anadolu

Mississippi Senate: Colom leads Hyde-Smith by ~1,100 votes, thousands of ballots to go, and there's no recount law

Facts

  • Democrat Scott Colom led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith 464,926 to 463,788 (+1,138) as of late Wednesday, with about 96% of the expected vote counted.
  • Still outstanding: about 3,600 mail ballots, which can arrive through Nov. 10, and an unknown number of affidavit (provisional) ballots. Estimates range from 15,000 (Colom's campaign) to 18,000 (unconfirmed reports). Counties must certify by Nov. 13.
  • Mississippi has no formal recount. After certification, the loser can request a "ballot box exam" and then go to court. The NRSC has demanded officials preserve all affidavit ballots, and the state GOP chair vowed to "fight like hell."
  • If Colom wins, he would be Mississippi's first Democratic senator elected since 1982 and its first Black senator since Reconstruction.

Left view

Mississippi Free Press reports that early affidavit batches are breaking heavily for Colom (69–29 in Lafayette County), and his campaign is already projecting victory. Democrats warn against GOP efforts to throw out provisional ballots.

Right view

Hyde-Smith's campaign says it's confident once "every legally cast vote" is verified, and Gov. Tate Reeves predicts she'll win. Republicans are focused on ballot integrity and curing rules. Magnolia Tribune notes the reports of 18,000 outstanding affidavit ballots are unconfirmed.

Watch for

The affidavit-curing process and any court fight over it. The Washington Post notes the state's lack of a recount mechanism makes litigation more likely than a re-tally. The seat doesn't decide control, but it sets the size of the new Democratic Senate majority.

Sources: ABC News Washington Post Magnolia Tribune Mississippi Free Press The Hill CNN

Newsom moves to empty California's death row, commuting all 548 sentences on his way out

Facts

  • Gov. Gavin Newsom said Thursday he will commute every death sentence in the state, 548 in all, to life without parole. Advocates call it the largest mass commutation in U.S. history.
  • For anyone with more than one felony conviction, the state constitution requires the California Supreme Court to sign off on clemency.
  • California hasn't executed anyone since 2006. Newsom imposed a moratorium in 2019 and dismantled San Quentin's chamber. Voters rejected repeal in 2016 (Prop. 62) and passed Prop. 66 to speed up executions.

Left view

The ACLU praised the move and called capital punishment racist and error-prone. It is also suing to strike down the state's death-penalty statute. Axios and KQED frame the move partly through Newsom's 2028 ambitions.

Right view

Fox News led with victims' families. Marc Klaas, whose daughter Polly's killer is on death row, called it a gift to murderers. San Luis Obispo DA Dan Dow called it an insult to victims, and LA DA Nathan Hochman noted that only voters or the Legislature can actually abolish the death penalty.

Watch for

How fast the state Supreme Court acts on the repeat-felon cases, prosecutors' legal challenges, and whether it becomes a 2028 attack line. Legally, new death sentences can still be handed down.

Sources: PBS / AP Fox News Axios KQED

Israel: Herzog names a prime-minister candidate Sunday, and Eisenkot's bloc has the numbers

Facts

  • President Isaac Herzog will announce Sunday whom he's tasking with forming a government. Parties backing Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot hold 67 of the Knesset's 120 seats, versus 46 for Netanyahu's camp.
  • In Gaza, Israeli strikes killed at least four more people Thursday despite the ceasefire. The UN condemned a settler takeover of Palestinian homes near Jericho.

Left view

Center-left Israeli and international coverage (e.g., Foreign Exchanges, Ahram) treats Netanyahu's likely ouster as overdue. It also stresses that Eisenkot, a former army chief, is a hawk and that a coalition built on very different parties may not hold together.

Right view

Netanyahu allies are floating a unity government with Eisenkot instead, and right-leaning Israeli outlets like the Jerusalem Post report protesters heckling Eisenkot. U.S. right-leaning coverage is thin. Mainstream U.S. outlets are mostly focused on the midterms.

Watch for

The designate gets 28 days, which can be extended, to form a coalition. A post-Netanyahu government could change Israel's stance on Iran just as Washington decides on strikes, and Vance has already called for "changing" the U.S.–Israel relationship.

Sources: Foreign Exchanges Anadolu Jerusalem Post Ahram

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: −4.36% Thursday. Dow: 51,521.28 (−1,834.84, −3.44%). Nasdaq: −5.52%, in correction. Futures are mixed ahead of the 8:30 ET jobs report, with tech bouncing (Nvidia and Micron up premarket) and the Dow lower.
  • Oil: Brent is back near $98 after Wednesday's ~8% plunge below $100. Iran headlines are moving it both ways, and U.S. crude is around $91.
  • Gas: The AAA national average is $4.10 (Nov. 5), down 12¢ in a week. That's still a record for November and more than $1 above a year ago.
  • Other: The 10-yr yield is ~4.84%. Gold is ~$4,080 and bitcoin ~$76K (−5%). Airbnb beat estimates and rose after hours. China blocked SoftBank's $5.4B deal for ABB's robotics unit, and Google announced a $17B data center in Wyoming.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Chris Kirk shot a bogey-free 63 (−9) to lead the World Wide Technology Championship in Los Cabos by one over Nick Dunlap and Zac Blair. Kirk is 110th in the FedEx Cup Fall standings and needs a top-100 finish to keep his card. Ryan Gerard and 19-year-old Blades Brown are at −6.
  • Tennis: At the Paris Masters, Taylor Fritz beat Arthur Fils 6-3 6-4, a blow to Fils's ATP Finals hopes. Ben Shelton survived Rinderknech in a third-set tiebreak, Alcaraz advanced on a Berrettini walkover, and Musetti was upset by Luca Van Assche. The WTA Finals start Saturday.
  • Squash: U.S. Open semis are today in Philadelphia. The men's are Asal vs. Elias and Abou Eleinen vs. Coll; the women's are Orfi vs. ElSherbini and El Hammamy vs. the Gohar/Ibrahim winner. Finals are Saturday.
  • WWE: SmackDown tonight is the go-home show before Saturday's Crown Jewel in Riyadh (noon ET). Riyadh Season moved the event to a new venue that hasn't been named yet. The card has Reigns vs. Zayn and Morgan vs. Green for the Crown Jewel titles, plus Cody vs. Orton in a Last Man Standing match.
  • Hockey: Jets 6, Canucks 2, with six different Winnipeg scorers. Also Devils 5, Blues 4 and Lightning 4, Blackhawks 1.
  • Soccer: Cristiano Ronaldo will retire from international football after Portugal's November games (Denmark Nov. 14, Wales Nov. 17). Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane extended with Bayern through 2029. In the Europa League, Ferencváros won 2-0 at Milan, Bournemouth came back to win 3-1 at Sparta Prague, Celtic beat Beşiktaş 3-2, and Dinamo Zagreb handed Sunderland its first league-phase loss.
  • Football: Jaguars 33, Ravens 10 on TNF. Trevor Lawrence threw for 242 yards with a 50-yard TD to Parker Washington, Cam Little hit four field goals, and the defense forced three turnovers. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano threw two picks in his first start, and Baltimore (4-5) has lost four straight. Jacksonville is 6-2.

item.title: Thu Nov 5, 2026 — The wave's full size comes into view: 54+ Senate seats, most governorships, Abbott and Collins out
item.description: The wave's full size comes into view: 54+ Senate seats, most governorships, Abbott and Collins out · Johnson steps aside, Trump promises vetoes, and a Dec. 11 shutdown deadline looms · Mississippi Senate race comes down to a sliver; Alaska still counting · Iran: Trump floats a "heavy hit" while Qatar pushes a deal; tankers burn near Hormuz
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

The wave's full size comes into view: 54+ Senate seats, most governorships, Abbott and Collins out

Facts

  • CBS News projects Democrats will hold at least 54 Senate seats in January after seven flips: Texas (Talarico over Paxton), North Carolina (Cooper), Ohio (Sherrod Brown), Maine (Troy Jackson over Collins, who conceded), Iowa (Turek), Kansas (Hamilton) and South Carolina (Annie Andrews). Mississippi and Alaska are still uncounted.
  • Democrats also won the House, and Fox's Chad Pergram says they could clear 240 seats despite GOP-drawn maps in Texas and Florida. A final count isn't in yet.
  • Democrats are set to hold a majority of governorships for the first time in 16 years (NBC News, Stateline), with five pickups in states Trump won. According to AFP, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott lost to Democrat Gina Hinojosa. Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia, Rob Sand won Iowa and Xavier Becerra won California.
  • Republican holds include Nebraska, where Pete Ricketts beat independent Dan Osborn, along with Florida, Montana, West Virginia and Tennessee.

Left view

Coverage reprinted from The Guardian has progressive groups claiming a mandate. Justice Democrats calls the result an endorsement of a "bold" agenda over a corporate one, and the Working Families Party says voters want both accountability for the administration and action on cost of living. Schumer, speaking to CBS, called it a "generational remake of the Senate map."

Right view

Fox News is collecting conservative post-mortems. Guy Benson (Washington Examiner) calls the night "catastrophic." The Federalist's Sean Davis calls it the worst GOP wipeout since 2006. Matt Walsh (Daily Wire) blames an unpopular Iran war and high prices. In a Washington Examiner op-ed, Michael Levin admits his red-wave call was wrong and blames Trump, and a National Review piece argues voters punished "shameless" politics.

Watch for

Fox's Pergram says the new majority will rest on moderates who won in Trump-leaning seats, not on progressives. At the Atlantic Council, Josh Lipsky warns that markets may be underpricing a January push that widens deficits. Overriding a veto would still take about 290 House votes and 67 in the Senate, so a big Democratic agenda is likely to stall at Trump's desk.

Sources: CBS News NBC News AFP Fox News Washington Examiner National Review Atlantic Council

Johnson steps aside, Trump promises vetoes, and a Dec. 11 shutdown deadline looms

Facts

  • Two people familiar with his decision told AP that Speaker Mike Johnson won't run for House Republican leader in the minority. Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan are the likely rivals in a vote expected next week, and Tom Emmer plans to run again for whip.
  • Democrats are expected to nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker on Jan. 3. He would be the first Black speaker.
  • On Fox, Trump congratulated Democrats and said Iran was "part of" the loss. He also said he'd veto bills he dislikes and blamed other Republicans, calling Abbott a "RINO." AFP reports the White House hinted at retribution against his political enemies.
  • Government funding runs out Dec. 11, and FISA Section 702 still needs reauthorization this month.

Left view

Schumer, speaking to CBS, promised "legislative razor wire" against Trump and said the "supplicant Senate" era is over. Progressive groups quoted by The Guardian want aggressive oversight from day one. Indivisible is urging senators to oppose Schumer's return as leader.

Right view

Fox's Pergram calls the GOP leadership race a test of Trump's hold on House Republicans, with Jordan pitching his record of fighting Democrats. Republicans quoted there expect investigations into Hegseth, RFK Jr., Noem and the Trump family's crypto ventures to be "brutal." They argue Democrats won by promising lower prices and now have to deliver.

Watch for

Pergram expects Democrats to avoid lame-duck deals and wait for January, which makes a December shutdown more likely. Lipsky (Atlantic Council) expects a debt-ceiling showdown in the first half of 2027 that ends in deals raising both spending and borrowing. Tariffs likely stay because Trump would veto any limits, though China policy could draw bipartisan support.

Sources: AP Fox News CBS News AFP The Guardian (via Finwire)

Mississippi Senate race comes down to a sliver; Alaska still counting

Facts

  • In Time's latest update, Democrat Scott Colom led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 1,138 votes (49.0% to 48.9%) with about 96% counted. Earlier counts reported by the Mississippi Free Press had the gap at a few dozen votes. AP hasn't called it.
  • Affidavit (provisional) ballots get counted within five business days, and mail ballots postmarked by Election Day count if they arrive within five days. Colom's campaign estimates about 15,000 affidavit ballots are outstanding.
  • A Colom win would make him the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Mississippi since 1982. In Alaska, Dan Sullivan (R) vs. Mary Peltola (D) is still a toss-up with a slow count.

Left view

The Mississippi Free Press, a progressive-leaning nonprofit, and Time both present a Colom win as a historic breakthrough in the Deep South and a sign of how far the wave reached.

Right view

Hyde-Smith's campaign told WLBT it is confident she wins once every legal ballot is counted. Republicans are focused on ballot verification, and NBC News reports the race could become a fight over individual ballots. Conservative coverage so far is light.

Watch for

Experts quoted by Time don't expect a result until late this week or next. A margin this thin points to legal fights over affidavit ballots and possibly a recount. Whatever happens, these two races only change how big the majority is, not who controls the Senate.

Sources: Time Mississippi Free Press NBC News WLBT ABC News

Iran: Trump floats a "heavy hit" while Qatar pushes a deal; tankers burn near Hormuz

Facts

  • Gulf News reports Trump told Fox the US may need to "do something large" against Iran. Reuters (via Business Recorder) reports he told the FT there are no immediate strike plans, and that he's ready for a deal but in no rush.
  • A senior Iranian official told Reuters the two sides are "still far from a deal." Qatari mediators carried a draft deal to Tehran Monday, and Doha says both sides are reviewing its proposals.
  • Iran's Revolutionary Guards say four tankers hit mines south of the Strait of Hormuz and are still burning. Tehran wants oil sanctions lifted, the US naval blockade ended and frozen funds released before it reopens the strait.
  • Iranian leaders are reading the US vote as a rebuke: negotiator Ghalibaf posted that Americans said "NO TO WAR." Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned against expecting a US policy shift.

Left view

Democrats and analysts aligned with them treat the midterms as a referendum on the war. The Atlantic Council's Leslie Shedd expects the new Congress to make curbing US military action a priority, and Tressa Guenov expects oversight of the Iran strikes and Caribbean operations. Left-leaning outlets haven't published much on Iran this morning beyond the election angle.

Right view

The right is split. Fox News reports Matt Walsh and Erick Erickson calling the war unpopular and a drag on the party, while the White House and Trump say they had support and voters balked only at gas prices. Hawks, per the Atlantic Council's Landon Derentz, expect Trump to put preventing a nuclear Iran ahead of the election result.

Watch for

Mediators expect replies from both sides within about 36 hours (Korea Herald, citing Reuters). Saxo Bank's Ole Hansen says Middle East crude shipments are recovering, about three-quarters of pre-war flows per Vortexa, which could lower pump prices later. A renewed strike or more mine hits would undo that quickly.

Sources: Gulf News Reuters (via Korea Herald) Reuters (via Business Recorder) Bloomberg Al Jazeera

Dow's best post-midterm day in 44 years — but the AI trade gets a political warning

Facts

  • The Dow jumped 1,569 points (+3.03%) Wednesday to 53,356, which Motley Fool calls the biggest post-midterm rally in 44 years. The S&P 500 rose 1.58% and the Nasdaq 1.44%.
  • TheStreet reports Brent fell roughly $10 at one point, briefly trading below $100, as traders priced in a de-escalation with Iran. It's up about 1% this morning.
  • Nasdaq 100 futures are down about 0.6% early Thursday. Qualcomm is off about 10% premarket after weak handset-chip guidance, and AI infrastructure names are slipping on worries about data-center pushback in states Democrats now control.
  • Wednesday's earnings: Apple rose about 6% on $114.5B in revenue, and CVS says it will split into two public companies by the first half of 2028.

Left view

Before the vote, Axios and others described local anger over data centers' power bills, water use and land as a Democratic campaign issue. Progressives now want the new majorities to scrutinize the AI build-out and Big Tech.

Right view

The Washington Examiner reported this fall that some Republicans were turning on data centers too, so the backlash isn't purely partisan. Markets' first read was that gridlock is a plus: blue-chip stocks rallied on the prospect of a Congress that can't pass much past Trump's veto.

Watch for

Reuters cites UBS saying data-center pauses could put about 30% of expected 2028 capacity additions at risk, though much of the chip slowdown is priced in. The Atlantic Council's Graham Brookie expects policy and market adjustments around AI to continue after a recent selloff of nearly $1 trillion in tech value.

Sources: TheStreet Motley Fool Reuters Axios Washington Examiner Bloomberg

Democrats' next fight is with each other: progressives vs. moderates, and Schumer's future

Facts

  • Progressives won several high-profile races, including Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate win. Moderates such as Adam Hamilton (Kansas) and Josh Turek (Iowa) flipped seats in Trump country.
  • Indivisible leaders Ezra Levin and Leah Greenberg are urging senators to oppose Schumer's bid for majority leader (The Guardian).
  • Schumer insists both wings ran on the same message, affordability and corruption, and says the caucus "will be united."

Left view

In The Guardian's reporting, DSA co-chair Ashik Siddique credits democratic socialists with moving opinion on ICE and Israel arms, and Progressive Democrats of America says progressives "won the battle" of primary season. The Working Families Party argues populists can win big margins.

Right view

Fox's Pergram expects Medicare for All, defunding ICE and cutting Israel aid to go nowhere and predicts a moderate-progressive split. A recent AEI commentary argued a wave built on the left could eventually hurt Democrats, and Yahoo reports Democratic moderates warning that a leftward lurch sets up a 2028 loss.

Watch for

Leadership elections and committee assignments are where the split will first show. The Atlantic Council expects likely chairs such as Adam Smith and Chris Coons to steer Ukraine and NATO policy. Some experts it quotes doubt Democrats will spend political capital on foreign aid while focused on affordability.

Sources: The Guardian (via Finwire) Fox News AEI Yahoo News Atlantic Council

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,688.62 (+1.58%). Dow: 53,356.12 (+3.03%). Nasdaq: 25,736.51 (+1.44%). Futures early Thursday: Dow +0.5%, S&P flat, Nasdaq 100 −0.6%.
  • Oil: Brent swung sharply Wednesday on Iran-deal hopes and briefly dipped below $100. It's up about 1% this morning near $101–102, with WTI near $95.
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.12 (Nov. 4), down from $4.36 in early October. Crude around $100 keeps it from falling much further.
  • Other: Qualcomm −10% and AppLovin +16% premarket. Apple +6% and Duolingo +19% Wednesday, while Amdocs −36% on a weak 2027 outlook. CVS plans to split in two by 2028.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The World Wide Technology Championship starts today at El Cardonal in Los Cabos (Nov. 5–8, $6M purse). Ben Griffin defends, Ryan Gerard is the top-ranked player in the field, and FedEx Cup Fall status is at stake.
  • Tennis: The Paris Masters (through Nov. 8) settles the last ATP Finals spots. Fils, Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar hold them provisionally, with de Minaur 64 points behind. The WTA Finals start Saturday at Indian Wells, with Rybakina defending and Sabalenka and Andreeva in the other group.
  • Squash: U.S. Open semis today in Philadelphia: Mostafa Asal vs. Diego Elias, and Amina Orfi vs. Nour ElSherbini. Finals are Saturday.
  • WWE: Crown Jewel is Saturday in Saudi Arabia, headlined by Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match. Ethan Page won the IC title from Chad Gable on Raw, and Cena announced a Dec. 14 "John Cena Classic" in Orlando.
  • Hockey: Adrian Kempe scored a hat trick in his return from injury as the Kings beat the Sharks 7–2, with four assists from Panarin. Also: Panthers 5, Blackhawks 3; Senators 2, Sabres 1; Kraken 2, Flames 1 on Beniers' OT breakaway.
  • Soccer: In the Champions League, Como beat Lens 9–1, matching the competition's record margin, and Fenerbahçe came back to beat Liverpool 3–2 for the Reds' first loss of the season. Real Madrid won late at AEK, and Arsenal and Man City also won. PSG lead the table.
  • Football: TNF tonight is Jaguars at Ravens (8:15 ET, Prime). Baltimore starts undrafted rookie QB Joe Fagnano after losing its top two quarterbacks.

item.title: Wed Nov 4, 2026 — Democrats sweep Congress, flipping both the Senate and the House
item.description: Democrats sweep Congress, flipping both the Senate and the House · Trump says the losses aren't on him as the GOP blame game starts · US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Hormuz talks stall; post-election strike plans in focus · California voters appear to reject the nation's first billionaire wealth tax
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Democrats sweep Congress, flipping both the Senate and the House

Facts

  • AP called the Senate for Democrats Tuesday night and the House early Wednesday. Hakeem Jeffries is now in line to become the first Black House speaker.
  • Senate flips include Ohio (Sherrod Brown over Sen. Jon Husted), Kansas (Adam Hamilton over Sen. Roger Marshall), Iowa (Josh Turek over Ashley Hinson), North Carolina (Roy Cooper), South Carolina (Annie Andrews over Darline Graham) and Texas, where James Talarico beat Ken Paxton to end the GOP's 32-year statewide winning streak there. Forbes reports Troy Jackson unseated Sen. Susan Collins in Maine. Democrats held Georgia (Ossoff), New Hampshire (Pappas) and Minnesota (Flanagan).
  • Republicans held Florida's Senate seat (Ashley Moody, about 51–48) and the governorship (Byron Donalds), plus Wyoming (Harriet Hageman). Some House races and ranked-choice counts in Maine and Alaska are still being tallied. Cook Political Report had projected Democratic House gains of up to about 25 seats.
  • Exit polls: about 60% of voters disapproved of Trump's job performance, and about 90% called cost of living a major factor. Gas averaged $4.15 on Election Day, the first Election Day above $4 (AAA, via Forbes).

Left view

The Guardian calls it a "blue wave" that hands Democrats real power to check Trump's agenda. MS NOW and Daily Kos treat the Texas and Kansas wins as signs the map has been redrawn, not just a normal midterm swing. AP's takeaways frame it as voters rebuking two years of a compliant GOP Congress. Democrats are already signaling oversight: likely Oversight chair Rep. Robert Garcia told Fox News Digital, "Lawyer up."

Right view

Fox News called it an "unprecedented blue wave," pointing to GOP losses with Hispanic, young, independent and rural voters, and led with Democrats' investigation threats. Ben Shapiro called it a "wipeout" and said the president was effectively on the ballot. The pro-Trump NY Post ran a "blue tsunami" front page that pinned the losses on him, and the WSJ editorial board called for a GOP reckoning. In The Free Press, editors asked whether this was a referendum on Trump or the usual second-term penalty.

Watch for

AP and PBS expect gridlock: Trump has vowed to veto Democratic priorities, and a Democratic Senate can now block his judicial and Supreme Court picks. Expect House subpoenas on the Iran war, DHS and administration ethics starting in January. Stalled spending fights and the debt limit move to the top of the lame-duck agenda. Analysts will also watch whether Democrats can hold voters who turned out against Trump rather than for the party (Free Press).

Sources: PBS/AP Forbes Fox News Guardian NBC News Houston Public Media Free Press

Trump says the losses aren't on him as the GOP blame game starts

Facts

  • In a phone interview with Fox News, Trump said he doesn't see the results as a hit on him, noted he "wasn't on the ballot," and said Republicans "just didn't inspire" voters. On Truth Social he said he would have won in a landslide.
  • CNN reports Trump blamed his own handpicked candidates. The NYT reports other Republicans put the blame squarely on him. A CBS headline says he acknowledged the Iran war played a part.
  • Going in, his approval sat near 38% in Nate Silver's tracker. Before the vote he floated a preemptive pardon for Elon Musk if Democrats won.

Left view

PBS says the results leave Trump with sharply reduced political capital at home and abroad. Rolling Stone and HuffPost focus on the deflection, saying a president who campaigned in nearly every battleground can't separate himself from the result. The common argument on the left, echoed in AP exit-poll coverage, is that the backlash was about prices, the war and corruption, not candidate quality.

Right view

The right is split. Loyalists on Fox emphasize Trump's point that he wasn't on the ballot and blame weak candidates and turnout, noting Georgia's GOP vote fell short of strategists' targets. The Murdoch papers and conservative commentators (NY Post, WSJ editorial board, Shapiro) argue the war, gas prices and tariffs were Trump's choices and that voters judged him. Caitlin Flanagan wrote in The Free Press that kitchen-table costs drove the anger.

Watch for

Lame-duck dynamics: watch whether GOP senators facing 2028 races start breaking with the White House on Iran war powers and tariffs. Leadership fights in the House GOP conference are likely. Also watch for aggressive executive actions and pardons before the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3.

Sources: CNN NYT PBS Hollywood Reporter (Shapiro) HuffPost (NY Post cover) Free Press

US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Hormuz talks stall; post-election strike plans in focus

Facts

  • US forces hit an Iranian anti-aircraft site on Qeshm Island, near the Strait of Hormuz, early this week. Officials called the strikes "defensive," a response to Iranian fire at a US aircraft. Trump called it "minor" and said it "wasn't war."
  • Iran's Mohsen Rezaei said the US reply to Tehran's seven-condition plan to reopen Hormuz was "not convincing." The conditions include lifting sanctions and ending the US naval blockade. Qatar says it is relaying proposals in real time and working toward an interim deal (Al Jazeera, CBS/Reuters).
  • US media reported CENTCOM had plans for strikes that could start as soon as today, with three carriers arriving in the region. Bloomberg reports Trump is now playing down that prospect after the midterm rout.
  • Shipping attacks continue: UKMTO reported a tanker hit by two projectiles off Oman, and a dhow attack in the strait killed one seafarer.

Left view

NPR and the Guardian frame the war, now in its ninth month, as a central driver of the GOP's losses, and Democrats are expected to push war-powers votes as soon as they take control. Critics such as John Mearsheimer, quoted by Al Jazeera, warn that another short bombing campaign won't achieve US goals and could pull the US into a longer war.

Right view

Fox News emphasizes the strikes' defensive nature and Trump's claim that Iran's forces have been "decapitated." AP reports Netanyahu is pressing Trump for a decisive post-election campaign. Trump told the FT the US is "getting everything we want," and he has also said US aid to Israel will end by year-end.

Watch for

Qatar expected feedback from both sides within about 36 hours. A deal to reopen Hormuz would likely knock oil sharply lower. Renewed large-scale strikes would push Brent back toward the $115+ levels seen in late October. Iran has hinted at hitting Gulf undersea cables or European targets if attacked.

Sources: Al Jazeera CBS News Bloomberg Fox News CNBC NPR

California voters appear to reject the nation's first billionaire wealth tax

Facts

  • With about half the expected vote counted, Prop. 40, a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state's roughly 200 billionaires, was losing about 44–56 (San José Inside). The union sponsor had projected about $100 billion for healthcare and education over five years.
  • Rival Prop. 42, which bans wealth taxes, was leading about 55–45. If it finishes with more yes votes than Prop. 40, it overrides the tax under the state constitution. Prop. 41 was trailing.
  • Opponents spent about $317 million, including $102 million from Sergey Brin. Gov. Newsom backed Prop. 42, while the state Democratic Party and labor federation backed Prop. 40.
  • Elsewhere, local measures on data centers were on ballots in Ohio, Illinois, Wisconsin and Florida. Ohio alone had 21, including outright bans in 13 municipalities (Forbes).

Left view

Progressive backers and the California Budget & Policy Center argue the state faces deep health-care cuts and that the measure was buried by record billionaire spending. Some on the left note that a Democratic wave still didn't carry a wealth tax, even in California.

Right view

Business groups and conservative outlets read the result as proof that even blue-state voters reject wealth taxes, warning that the threat alone was pushing founders and capital out of California. They see Newsom's support for Prop. 42 as confirmation. Coverage so far comes mostly from California outlets; national right-leaning coverage is thin.

Watch for

California counts slowly, so final margins could take weeks. Expect legal fights over how competing measures interact if margins tighten. The data-center votes are an early test of local backlash against AI infrastructure, a theme Amundi's Aidan Yao flagged as a market risk.

Sources: San José Inside CalMatters SF Standard KPBS

Wall Street whipsaws on the blue sweep, then steadies

Facts

  • Overnight, Nasdaq-100 futures fell as much as 2.4% and S&P 500 futures 1.4% as the Democratic sweep became clear. Asian markets slid too. By early Wednesday, US futures had recovered to small gains (Reuters via Yahoo Finance; The National).
  • Tuesday's close: S&P 500 +0.36%, ending a three-day losing streak; Nasdaq +0.83% on a chip rebound; Dow −197 points, dragged down by Apple (StockTitan, Motley Fool).
  • Apple fell 1.9% (about $94 billion in market value) despite record September-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, after warning that rising memory-chip costs will squeeze holiday-quarter margins.

Left view

Democratic-leaning analysts argue divided government has historically been fine for stocks. They say a Congress that can rein in tariffs and the Iran war could reduce the biggest sources of inflation risk.

Right view

Market-focused conservatives worry about tougher tech and AI regulation, an end to further tax cuts, and investigations that add policy uncertainty. Futures falling hardest in the Nasdaq reflects that concern.

Watch for

Amundi's Aidan Yao told Reuters the midterms are less a referendum on Trump than on AI: if the AI trade faces restrictions, the outlook for growth, inflation and Fed policy gets much murkier. The 10-year yield near 4.9–5% and gold above $4,000 suggest investors are still hedging.

Sources: Reuters/Yahoo Finance The National StockTitan Motley Fool

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: +0.36% Tuesday. Dow: −197 pts (−0.38%). Nasdaq: +0.83%. Futures early Wed: S&P ~7,611 (+0.2%), Dow ~52,121 (+0.4%), Nasdaq ~28,365 (+0.2%) after an overnight dip.
  • Oil: Brent settled at $103.60 Tuesday (−1.1%) on deal hopes after briefly topping $105 on the Qeshm strike. WTI December was around $96.50 early Wednesday.
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.15 on Election Day, down from $4.17 Monday and well below the $4.56 May peak. It was $2.98 when the Iran war began Feb. 28.
  • Other: 10-year Treasury about 4.91–4.95%. Gold up roughly 2.6% to about $4,044. VIX eased to about 19.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: PGA Tour's World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico (Ben Griffin defends). The DP World Tour playoffs continue with the Abu Dhabi Championship (Aaron Rai defends). LPGA is at the Toto Japan Classic. LIV's 2026 season is over.
  • Tennis: At the Paris Masters, Djokovic came back to beat Valentin Vacherot 6-7, 7-5, 6-1. Shelton, Fritz, Tommy Paul, Tien and Michelsen also advanced, and Berrettini beat Nakashima. The WTA Finals start Nov. 8 at Indian Wells, moved from Riyadh over Iran-war security concerns.
  • Squash: US Open in Philadelphia reaches the quarterfinals today: Asal vs. Makin and Mohamed ElShorbagy vs. Elias for the men; Orfi vs. Subramaniam and ElSherbini vs. Kennedy for the women. Sana Ibrahim upset top American Olivia Weaver 3-0. Finals are Saturday.
  • WWE: On Raw in Brooklyn, Ethan Page beat Chad Gable for the Intercontinental title. John Cena announced the first John Cena Classic (Dec. 14, Orlando), with Cody Rhodes as the first entrant. Sami Zayn hit Roman Reigns with a Helluva Kick ahead of their Crown Jewel title match.
  • Hockey: Tuesday: Devils beat Oilers 4-3 in OT, Ducks 5, Canucks 4; Mammoth 3, Maple Leafs 2; Golden Knights 3, Penguins 2. Edmonton is 11-2-2.
  • Soccer: Champions League Matchday 4: PSG crushed Villarreal 6-0, Bayern won 2-0 at Atlético, Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0, Inter won 3-0 at Feyenoord, and Man United came back to beat Roma 3-2. Galatasaray beat Stuttgart 2-0.
  • Football: In Week 8, Commanders beat Eagles 27-10 on SNF, Bills routed Ravens 36-10 (Lamar Jackson likely headed to IR with a thumb injury), Broncos edged Chiefs 28-24, and Cardinals beat Cowboys 33-30 in OT. Week 9 opens Thursday with Jaguars at Ravens.

item.title: Tue Nov 3, 2026 — Election Day: polls are open, 57 million have already voted, and House and Senate control is on the line
item.description: Election Day: polls are open, 57 million have already voted, and House and Senate control is on the line · US hits Iran's Qeshm Island on election eve in "defensive" strikes as a Doha draft deal hangs in the balance · Supreme Court refuses DOJ bid to wall off 20,000 California mail ballots · Ballot measures: California's billionaire tax (Prop 40) slips in final polls
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Election Day: polls are open, 57 million have already voted, and House and Senate control is on the line

Facts

  • All 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are on the ballot, along with about 145 statewide ballot measures. More than 57 million people voted early, according to the University of Florida Voting Lab (CBS News). Republicans hold the Senate 53-47 and have a razor-thin House majority.
  • Final New York Times/Siena polls show Democrats ahead in Michigan (El-Sayed 53, Rogers 42), Texas (Talarico 50, Paxton 43) and Kansas (Hamilton 49, Marshall 44). Other final polls show Maine (Jackson 51, Collins 45), Ohio (Brown 49, Husted 44), Alaska (Peltola 48, Sullivan 46) and Iowa (Turek 48, Hinson 47) within single digits. Nebraska's Ricketts and independent Osborn are tied at 49 (Forbes roundup). Silver Bulletin's generic-ballot average is D+8.9.
  • CBS's Battleground Tracker projects 229 Democratic House seats, with a range of 215-237. Kalshi bettors give Democrats about a 94% chance of winning the House.
  • Trump closed his campaign Monday in Washington, saying Republicans had a "very strong shot." He also acknowledged that the sitting president usually doesn't win the midterms.

Left view

Mainstream and left-leaning coverage frames the vote as a verdict on Trump's second term. NPR and CBS emphasize cost-of-living pressure and an unpopular Iran war, and the Forbes/NYT poll roundup points to Democratic leads in red states like Texas and Kansas. Democrats on the ground in Michigan argue that Haley Stevens's defection is backfiring. CBS quotes Rep. Debbie Dingell saying the endorsement is "galvanizing" voters behind El-Sayed.

Right view

Fox News presents the night as a turnout test for a GOP playing defense. It quotes RNC chair Joe Gruters: "If our voters turn out, we win." It also notes that Fox's own Power Rankings moved Kansas to toss-up, and it flags the ballot-integrity measures (voter ID, noncitizen voting) on the ballot in 11 states. The Washington Examiner's Guy Benson has warned for weeks that the GOP faces a "reckoning" while noting Democrats remain unpopular themselves.

Watch for

Kentucky's 6th District, which Trump won by about 15 points, is an early bellwether (Fox). Alaska's ranked-choice count could take days or weeks, and Maine also uses ranked choice. If the Senate comes down to Alaska, expect a certification fight there. Markets have largely priced in a split Congress. A Democratic sweep would put tariffs, Iran war funding and oversight at the center of 2027.

Sources: CBS News Forbes (NYT/Siena) CNN Fox News Washington Examiner

US hits Iran's Qeshm Island on election eve in "defensive" strikes as a Doha draft deal hangs in the balance

Facts

  • US officials told the Wall Street Journal, CBS and others that American forces carried out "limited defensive strikes" Monday night on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz. Officials said the strikes answered Revolutionary Guard fire on a US aircraft. Qeshm reportedly hosts an underground missile facility and a naval base (RFE/RL). Iranian media reported explosions there and in Bandar Lengeh. No casualties were reported.
  • The WSJ says this is one of a string of previously undisclosed limited strikes, kept quiet to avoid signaling a return to full-scale war. The IRGC claims it captured two US reconnaissance drones and downed an MQ-9 (Al Jazeera).
  • Asked whether he'd strike Iran after the midterms, Trump said "No." He posted that a deal "could happen" and that Iran "wants a settlement." Per the WSJ, though, US officials told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign shortly after the election. AP reports Netanyahu is pushing for exactly that.
  • Iran's foreign ministry says "the ball is in the US court." Tehran says Hormuz can reopen within two days if the US lifts its naval blockade and ends hostilities. Separately, a vessel off Oman was hit by an "unidentified aerial object," killing one Indian crew member. UKMTO logged a record 30 attacks on shipping in October (CBS).

Left view

Common Dreams and MS NOW lead with the timing: strikes hours before the vote, after Trump said there would be none before the midterms. NIAC's Jamal Abdi calls it an unauthorized war waged in secret and urges Congress to cut funding. Sen. Chris Murphy, citing a classified briefing, called a reported post-election plan to resume major attacks "insane." NPR's Morning Edition reports Iran is preparing for renewed attacks after the midterms.

Right view

Fox News's live coverage frames the strikes as protecting US forces and shipping while talks continue. It pairs them with Trump's "give them the hammer" warning and his reported preference, per Axios, to let negotiations play out. The Jerusalem Post reports, citing officials, that the strikes followed Iran downing a US drone. It treats them as calibrated, not a policy shift.

Watch for

Oil gave back part of Monday's 7% plunge, with Brent near $106-107. Emirates NBD's Daniel Richards says the strikes "renewed uncertainty" around the diplomatic opening. Swissquote's Ipek Ozkardeskaya notes the election can shift expectations but can't reopen shipping lanes on its own. A signed deal that ends the blockade is the big downside risk for crude, and a post-election air campaign the big upside one. Gas prices follow with a lag of a week or two.

Sources: CBS News RFE/RL Al Jazeera Common Dreams MS NOW Fox News Jerusalem Post The National

Supreme Court refuses DOJ bid to wall off 20,000 California mail ballots

Facts

  • On Monday the Supreme Court denied the administration's emergency request to make California set aside mail ballots from about 20,000 people DOJ says are likely noncitizens. CBS describes a one-line unsigned order with no noted dissents. Fox reports Justice Elena Kagan acted on it without referring it to the full court.
  • DOJ had lost at every level. US District Judge David Carter called the government's identification process "rife with uncertainty and errors," and a divided 9th Circuit panel declined to intervene. More than 6 million California mail ballots have been returned.
  • Fox News also reports that Chief Judge James Boasberg in Washington said it was "likely" the administration violated the Constitution by taking over election duties from states and Congress. He blocked further federal mail-ballot requests to California. (Other outlets reviewed hadn't yet reported this.)

Left view

CBS, OPB and KPBS (AP) emphasize state officials' warning that the federal list is error-prone and could disenfranchise eligible citizens. They present the ruling as courts shutting down federal interference in state-run elections on the eve of the vote.

Right view

Fox News centers DOJ's argument that once illegal ballots are counted, the harm "is impossible to remedy." It notes the administration sought only to preserve the ballots, not cancel them, and highlights Judge Patrick Bumatay's 9th Circuit dissent. It also points out that California's 52 House seats matter to the majority math.

Watch for

The order ends the pre-election fight but not the underlying lawsuit, so DOJ can still contest the ballots after the count. Combined with the Alaska certification case, it sets the template for post-election litigation if close races hinge on contested ballots.

Sources: CBS News Fox News Axios The Hill OPB (AP)

Ballot measures: California's billionaire tax (Prop 40) slips in final polls

Facts

  • Prop 40 would levy a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of roughly 200-250 California billionaires, with most of the money going to offset Medi-Cal and other health cuts. It's backed by SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West.
  • Support has eroded. PPIC's late-October likely-voter poll has it at 46% yes and 52% no, down from 52% support a month earlier (CalMatters). UC Berkeley IGS has it at 42-50 (KQED).
  • Opponents have raised over $205 million, including at least $102 million from Sergey Brin. Billionaire-backed Props 41 and 42 would nullify the tax if they get more votes, and Prop 42 polls at 51%.
  • Elsewhere: Washington votes on a millionaires' tax, and voter-ID or noncitizen-voting measures are on the ballot in 11 states (Fox News).

Left view

Supporters quoted by CalMatters argue that a clear majority still backs a "modest, one-time tax" on the very richest to keep health care affordable. KQED's poll coverage attributes the slide to a lopsided money fight. Berkeley IGS's Mark DiCamillo says the no side only has to "raise doubts." NPR's Planet Money notes economists studying the tax reached sharply different revenue estimates.

Right view

National Review calls the measure "fiscal self-sabotage," arguing that billionaire flight could cost California billions in ongoing income-tax revenue, more than the one-time tax raises. Tax Notes warns that a "one-time" levy would set a lasting precedent.

Watch for

Political Wire and others see Prop 40 as a 2028 test of the Democratic left's wealth-tax pitch. If it passes but Prop 42 gets more votes, expect it to land in court. California's count runs for weeks, so a close result won't be known tonight.

Sources: CalMatters KQED NPR Planet Money National Review Tax Notes Political Wire

Israel: Arab parties back Eisenkot ahead of Herzog's coalition talks Wednesday

Facts

  • The Joint List (11 seats) and Ra'am (8) say they'll recommend Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister. Added to his bloc's 48, that's 67 of 120 seats, against Netanyahu's 53 (Al Jazeera, Jerusalem Post).
  • Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen says his party won't join a government while the West Bank occupation continues but would vote with one. That opens the door to a minority government.
  • Results are certified Wednesday, when President Herzog opens consultations. The nominee gets 28 days, extendable by 14, and the Knesset is sworn in Nov. 10. Herzog: the results "are an established fact."

Left view

Al Jazeera notes Eisenkot, Bennett and Liberman have all ruled out Arab parties in government, while Labor's Yair Golan urges working with them. It frames Netanyahu's unproven fraud claims as a bid to delegitimize a Jewish-Arab majority.

Right view

Likud warns that Zionist parties relying on the Arab bloc would be "dangerous to Israel" and has suggested it borders on treason (via Al Jazeera). The Jerusalem Post lists outcomes from a unity government to a new election and reports Likud and Ra'am remain in contact. US right-leaning coverage is thin.

Watch for

The opposition's first move may be ousting Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana (Likud). An Eisenkot-led government would likely be more cautious about joining renewed US strikes on Iran. That ties the outcome directly to the Hormuz story above.

Sources: Al Jazeera Jerusalem Post NBC News CNBC

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: −0.5% Monday as the tech sell-off continued. Dow: +0.41% to 51,983.98 as oil's plunge lifted cyclicals. Nasdaq: about −1.1% (Yahoo Finance). After the close, Apple and Palantir both beat estimates but slid about 3% after hours. Apple posted $114.5B in revenue (+12%) but missed on China and guided margins light. Palantir's revenue rose 96%, and it raised full-year guidance to about $8.53B (TipRanks).
  • Oil: Brent settled at $104.77 Monday, down about 7.5% on deal hopes, then bounced toward $106-107 early Tuesday after the Qeshm strikes. WTI is near $98 (The National, CNBC).
  • Gas: The AAA national average was $4.16 Monday, down about 14¢ in a week and 23¢ in a month. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan says it could dip under $4 within a week "barring a course change" (Yahoo Finance).
  • Other: October ISM manufacturing came in at 55.5, beating estimates. The 10-year yield is about 4.89%, gold about $3,922 (−1.2%) and Bitcoin about $76,400 (−2%). Ahead: election results tonight, AMD, Qualcomm and ARM earnings this week, and the October jobs report Friday.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The PGA Tour's fall swing heads to Cabo for the World Wide Technology Championship at El Cardonal, Nov. 5-8, a week after Andrew Novak's Mexico Open win (Golf Channel).
  • Tennis: At the Paris Masters, 20-year-old Rafael Jodar marked his top-10 debut by beating Alejandro Tabilo 6-2, 6-3, and he faces Casper Ruud next. Musetti edged Hurkacz in two tiebreaks. Today Novak Djokovic plays Basel champion Valentin Vacherot, with the last ATP Finals spots on the line this week (Tennis Majors).
  • Squash: In US Open round 2, veteran Mohamed ElShorbagy upset No. 6 Mohamad Zakaria in four games. Nour ElSherbini survived Amanda Sobhy in five, and Asal, Elias, Makin and Orfi advanced. Tonight Paul Coll, Hania El Hammamy and Nouran Gohar play their round-2 matches (PSA).
  • WWE: Ethan Page beat Chad Gable for the Intercontinental title on Raw in Brooklyn, ending Gable's reign at 92 days. John Cena announced the "John Cena Classic" for Dec. 14 in Orlando, with a spinner-style title, and named Cody Rhodes the first entrant. Crown Jewel in Riyadh is Saturday, with Rhodes vs. Orton in a Last Man Standing match and Sami Zayn defending the WWE title (SI).
  • Hockey: Cutter Gauthier had his second career hat trick as the Ducks came back to beat Ottawa 6-3 on Sunday (NHL.com). Kochetkov (10-0) and McDavid's season-opening assist streak remain the storylines entering a full Tuesday slate.
  • Soccer: Champions League matchday 4 starts today. Atlético vs. Bayern, Villarreal vs. PSG, Barcelona vs. Aston Villa and Man United vs. Roma all kick off at 3pm ET. On Wednesday, Arsenal visits Slavia Prague, Liverpool visits Fenerbahçe and City visits Leipzig (Dimers).
