item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Midterms eve: 54 million ballots in, Trump closes in Iowa and Kansas, and Maine is tied

Facts

  • Polls open tomorrow, Nov. 3. The University of Florida early-vote tracker counts more than 54 million ballots already cast, up from about 50 million on Oct. 31 (CBS News). Republicans go in holding the House 219-214 and the Senate 53-47.
  • Democrats lead the RealClearPolling generic ballot 51.5% to 43.1%. CBS News polling gives Democrats an edge for the House. CBS lists Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas and Alaska as Senate toss-ups and has moved South Carolina to lean GOP. A new Fox News poll has Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson tied 49-49 in Maine.
  • Trump ended his campaign with a roughly two-hour rally in Dubuque, Iowa, and a 90-minute one in Salina, Kansas, telling the Kansas crowd it was his last stop. AP reports hundreds left Salina before he finished. He has held more than two dozen rallies in 19 states since October.
  • Late items: Barack Obama endorsed Democrat Charles Booker against Rep. Andy Barr in Kentucky. In California, a federal judge ordered the Justice Department to stop threatening election officials over alleged noncitizen ballots (CBS News).

Left view

PBS NewsHour and AP-syndicated coverage cast Tuesday as a referendum on Trump's second term. They note his approval is at its second-term low and that he spent the final weekend defending red states rather than contesting ones Biden won. Al Jazeera's pre-vote guide quotes pollster Natalie Jackson saying the environment favors Democrats because of Trump's unpopularity and cost-of-living pressure.

Right view

Fox News's live coverage centers on Democratic infighting in Michigan and on Collins's charge that Chuck Schumer is running "outright lies" against her. GOP strategist Doug Heye told Al Jazeera that Republican voters may be undercounted by pollsters.

Watch for

Jackson says she's "fairly confident" Democrats take the House while the Senate is unclear. Indiana and Kentucky close first tomorrow evening. Alaska's ranked-choice count and several close races could take days. Markets are treating a split Congress as the base case. A Democratic House would make oversight, tariffs and Iran war funding the main 2027 fights.

Sources: CBS News AP via Yahoo PBS NewsHour Al Jazeera Fox News

Michigan shock: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over El-Sayed

Facts

  • Rep. Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost the August Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday. She said she remains a Democrat and will back Democrats in about 90% of her races. The seat is open because Democratic Sen. Gary Peters is retiring.
  • The break followed a fight over a Rebellion PAC ad linking US military aid to Israel with grocery prices. Stevens called the ad antisemitic. El-Sayed said his campaign didn't make it and that he disagrees with it. Rep. Debbie Dingell then asked Stevens not to attend a Sunday unity event, calling her presence "way too distracting."
  • Schumer called it a "despicable betrayal." Stevens's chief of staff of eight years and several staffers resigned. El-Sayed's campaign says it raised more than $1.2 million afterward. Trump praised Stevens, invited her to join the GOP, and called El-Sayed a "jihadist." El-Sayed would be the first Muslim US senator.
  • More than 1.8 million Michiganders had voted before the endorsement. Reuters reports polls show El-Sayed has largely consolidated Democratic support.

Left view

NPR and Al Jazeera focus on the timing: less than 48 hours out, and after Stevens said midweek she still wanted El-Sayed to win. Al Jazeera notes an AIPAC-affiliated super PAC spent tens of millions on Stevens in the primary. Progressive figures were harsher. Fox News collected posts from Mehdi Hasan, Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur, with Hasan calling Stevens "evil."

Right view

The Washington Examiner frames the endorsement as a sign of a broader problem in the Democratic Party. It leads with Stevens's claim that El-Sayed has been "getting angrier and angrier" and that pro-Israel Democrats are being made to feel unwelcome. Fox News calls it a "bombshell," quotes the RNC on Rogers's cross-party appeal, and notes GOP Rep. Anna Paulina Luna offered Stevens her office's help, praising her for "putting country over party."

Watch for

Stevens beat El-Sayed in Wayne and Oakland counties, drawing Black and Jewish Democrats. Turnout there is the test of whether her move costs El-Sayed anything. Celinda Lake, a strategist working with El-Sayed's campaign, expects a "really close" race that hinges on turnout. Michigan is one of the seats that could decide Senate control.

Sources: Al Jazeera NPR CNBC Washington Examiner Fox News

Iran: negotiators leave Doha with a draft deal in circulation; Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz in two days

Facts

  • Iran's negotiators left Doha on Sunday. An official told Reuters the departure wasn't due to problems and that a draft proposal for a US deal is circulating, with a follow-up meeting possible. Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi relayed messages to Washington through Qatar.
  • FM Abbas Araqchi told Al Jazeera the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within two days of a deal, down from Iran's earlier seven-day plan. Spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said nothing reopens unless the US naval blockade ends and Iran's other demands are met. Qatar's Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports preliminary understandings on nuclear issues, shipping and financial incentives, with China and Russia as guarantors.
  • Trump says there will be no new attacks before the vote and that the US is "not in that much of a hurry." In Dubuque he said "at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer." Per Axios, Netanyahu pressed him in a "tough" call Saturday to strike right after the midterms. Trump described the call as "very good."
  • UKMTO reported a tanker hit by two unknown projectiles off Saudi Arabia, with all crew safe.

Left view

NPR, reporting from Bahrain, focuses on Gulf anxiety. It questions the administration's line that Iran is "essentially finished," noting that the Revolutionary Guard can still hit Gulf states and has threatened undersea internet cables. The Guardian reported the two-day timetable as agreed. The Times of Israel called it conditional, a gap worth noting.

Right view

Fox News's live coverage stresses Trump's leverage: Iran's navy and air force are largely destroyed, and only "one or two" nuclear sites are left. It treats fuel prices tied to the war as a midterm liability that renewed strikes could reshape. The Washington Examiner has argued that operational signals point toward more strikes regardless of the talks.

Watch for

Forbes's risk checklist puts Hormuz traffic at roughly two transits a day against a pre-war average of 138. War-risk insurance runs 6-10% of hull value, against about 0.25% before the war. A deal that ends the blockade would be the single biggest downside catalyst for oil. A post-election strike would likely send Brent back toward its October highs. Iran's army says any new round would last longer than the last.

Sources: Reuters NPR The Media Line NewsCord (coverage comparison) Fox News Forbes

Alaska: judge tosses DOJ bid to block Senate certification; Sullivan says he'll accept the result

Facts

  • US District Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed the Justice Department's suit on Sunday in a 20-page order. The suit sought to delay certification if GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan loses. She ruled DOJ lacked standing because it couldn't show a court order would fix its alleged injury. She added that it offered no "workable plan" to isolate ballots cast for the second "Daniel J. Sullivan" without breaking ballot secrecy.
  • DOJ says it will appeal to the 9th Circuit. Separately, it is running a criminal probe into how Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. got on the ballot and has subpoenaed several Democratic officials. No one has been charged.
  • Sen. Sullivan told CNN he'll accept the results but accused Mary Peltola's camp of cheating. He wouldn't say whether he'd back a refusal to certify, which Gov. Mike Dunleavy has floated. Peltola denies any role and calls the fight a distraction from high prices.

Left view

NPR, MS NOW and the Anchorage Daily News headline it as Trump's attempt to block results being rejected. MS NOW stood out for highlighting Sullivan's pledge to accept the outcome. Peltola's campaign frames the lawsuit as a pre-emptive challenge to a race Republicans fear losing.

Right view

Fox News stresses that the case was dismissed on procedural grounds without reaching DOJ's core claim. It leans on the New York Times report that people tied to Peltola's campaign helped recruit the spoiler, and gives prominence to the appeal and criminal probe. Newsweek's headline emphasizes that the judge was Obama-appointed.

Watch for

Alaska's ranked-choice tally means a result could take days or weeks. If Peltola wins narrowly, expect a 9th Circuit appeal and a fight over whether Dunleavy certifies. That could leave a seat in limbo during the battle for Senate control.

Sources: CBS News Al Jazeera NPR Fox News Washington Examiner NewsCord

Israel: officials say election results stand despite Likud's "stolen" claim; certification due this week

Facts

  • Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48, so neither has a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats. Eisenkot's bloc plus the Arab parties would reach 67.
  • Likud alleges, without public evidence, that Arab parties "stole" the vote, including with Qatari money. Qatar calls it disinformation. Central Elections Committee chair Noam Sohlberg said in a joint video with the Shin Bet chief and attorney general that even if the suspicions are borne out, they wouldn't undermine the result.
  • Police arrested three activists allegedly carrying cash to bribe voters and linked them to Ra'am. Two were released Sunday, one under house arrest. Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas called the arrests undemocratic.

Left view

Al Jazeera and the Times of Israel present the fraud claim as groundwork to delegitimize a possible Jewish-Arab government. The Times of Israel argues Netanyahu may be positioning for a repeat election in which Arab turnout drops. Eisenkot accuses him of a coordinated campaign to discredit the results.

Right view

The Jerusalem Post's coverage relays Likud's case: hundreds of testimonies, cash-filled envelopes tied to Ra'am, and banned voter-mobilization software, which Likud calls a "grave blow to Israeli democracy." The Post notes the allegations are unverified. US right-leaning coverage of the dispute is thin, and Israeli right-wing parties are making the case themselves.

Watch for

Once results are certified, President Isaac Herzog nominates someone to try to form a government. Watch whether Eisenkot drops his earlier refusal to partner with Arab parties. That decision affects Israel's posture toward any renewed US strikes on Iran.

Sources: Al Jazeera Times of Israel Jerusalem Post JTA

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: futures +0.4-0.5% premarket after a down week; Friday close 7,578.97. Dow: futures +0.4-0.6% (Friday 51,785.82). Nasdaq: Nasdaq-100 futures +0.8% after the index's worst month since March 2025 (-5.2% in October), driven by disappointing AI-spending guidance from Alphabet and Microsoft (TipRanks, Yahoo Finance).
  • Oil: WTI fell about 4% to roughly $99.50, back under $100. Brent fell about 4% to roughly $108.50 on signs of a US-Iran diplomatic path (Reuters, TipRanks).
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.17 (Nov. 1), down from about $4.22 a week ago and $4.36 in early October. AAA says crude above $100 has limited further declines; today's drop under $100 gives some room.
  • Other: 10-year yield about 4.91%. Gold about $3,913. Bitcoin is near $78,000 after Binance resumed withdrawals following last week's $6.3B hack. This week: ISM manufacturing today, Apple and Palantir after the close, then AMD, Qualcomm, ARM, Uber and McDonald's. Election Day is Tuesday and the October jobs report comes Friday.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Andrew Novak won the VidantaWorld Mexico Open at 25-under, five clear of Steven Fisk and Kristoffer Ventura, for his first solo PGA Tour title. The win comes with a two-year exemption and spots in the Players and PGA Championship (Golf.com).
  • Tennis: Unseeded Valentin Vacherot came back to beat Jiri Lehecka 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 for the Basel title, his second career title after Shanghai 2025 (ESPN/AP). The Paris Masters starts today.
  • Squash: The US Open is underway in Philadelphia (Nov. 1-7). Top seeds Mostafa Asal and Amina Orfi, plus Paul Coll, Diego Elias, Hania El Hammamy and Nour ElSherbini, all won in straight games. Joel Makin and Nouran Gohar needed five (PSA).
  • WWE: Raw is at Barclays Center tonight as part of a Raw/SmackDown double. The card includes a John Cena announcement, a Roman Reigns appearance, Chad Gable vs. Ethan Page for the IC title, and Penta, Je'Von Evans and Dragon Lee vs. The Vision. Crown Jewel is Saturday in Riyadh.
  • Hockey: Pyotr Kochetkov made 26 saves as Carolina blanked Winnipeg 7-0. He's 10-0 to open the season, and the Jets have lost nine straight. McDavid had a goal and an assist in Edmonton's 4-1 win over the Rangers, extending his record season-opening assist streak to 15 games. He leads the league with 39 points (NHL.com, ESPN).
  • Soccer: Kai Havertz scored, set up by Declan Rice after an Alisson giveaway, as Arsenal won 1-0 at Anfield. Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar for Liverpool. The win puts Arsenal top of the Premier League (NBC Sports, VAVEL).
  • Football: Jayden Daniels and Washington rallied from 10-0 down to beat the Eagles 27-10 on Sunday Night Football. Philadelphia (2-6) has lost six straight without Jalen Hurts. The Giants (4-2-1) lead the NFC East, and Dallas (3-5) blew a lead to Arizona (Yahoo Sports).

item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Midterms, 2 days out: 51 million ballots cast, Democrats hold a high-single-digit generic lead, Senate still a coin flip

Facts

  • More than 51 million Americans have already voted ahead of Tuesday, Nov. 3. All 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are on the ballot. Democrats need a net gain of three House seats and four Senate seats to flip both chambers.
  • The RealClearPolling average has Democrats ahead 51.5% to 43.1% on the generic ballot. The final PBS News/NPR/Marist poll (Oct. 19-20) had Democrats up 52-44 among likely voters, Trump's approval at 40%, and cost of living (34%) narrowly ahead of preserving democracy (33%) as the top issue.
  • Senate control likely turns on Michigan, Texas, Kansas, Iowa, North Carolina and Alaska. A Washington Post-Schar School poll released Saturday has Democrat Adam Hamilton up 52-43 over GOP Sen. Roger Marshall in Kansas, which hasn't elected a Democratic senator since 1932. Emerson has that race at 50-47.
  • Trump holds in-person rallies in Iowa and Kansas today after canceling both and then reversing course Friday. In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed campaigns in Detroit and Southfield against Republican Mike Rogers in a race strategist Celinda Lake calls "really close."

Left view

PBS NewsHour frames the race as a referendum driven by disapproval of Trump, with that disapproval pushing early turnout. Coverage summarized by Al Jazeera ties voters' cost-of-living anger to tariffs and the Iran war. Its story also notes rising Islamophobic attacks on El-Sayed.

Right view

The Washington Examiner's live coverage stresses GOP skepticism of the polls showing Democrats competitive in Kansas and Texas. It points to past polling misses in red-state Senate races. The Federalist argues the Senate polls may be overstating Democrats, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune has predicted Republicans will outperform the polls and keep the chamber.

Watch for

Pollster Natalie Jackson told Al Jazeera that Democrats are fairly likely to take the House but the Senate is unclear, and that polls may undercount Republicans. Indiana and Kentucky close first Tuesday evening, and close races (Alaska above all) may take days. Markets are treating a split Congress as the base case. A Democratic House would make tariff and war-funding fights the 2027 storyline.

Sources: Al Jazeera PBS NewsHour Washington Examiner The Federalist TIME

"If we don't win, there's no money": Trump ties disaster aid, veterans' claims and E15 to GOP wins

Facts

  • An AP review documents Trump repeatedly linking federal help to Republican victories. In North Carolina, he said he'd settle the remaining Camp Lejeune veterans' claims if Republicans win Congress, adding "if we don't win, there's no money." In September he tied Hurricane Helene recovery money to Senate candidate Michael Whatley's election, then said he was joking.
  • In Kansas, Trump said he'd make year-round E15 ethanol sales permanent with Sen. Roger Marshall but not if Democrat Adam Hamilton wins. He also suggested a reelected Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) and Ohio Democratic governor candidate Amy Acton would get less help.
  • CNN counts transactional promises of this kind in roughly half the states with key Senate contests.
  • The White House says Trump simply wants a GOP majority to keep delivering on taxes, drug prices and immigration.

Left view

CNN calls it an effort to buy votes with taxpayer money. Ossoff called it a "losing strategy" of insulting and threatening voters, and NC Democrat Roy Cooper called the Camp Lejeune threat insulting. Coverage collected by NewsCord, including MS NOW and NYT syndication, ties it to a broader pattern of using federal power for retribution.

Right view

Right-leaning coverage of this story is thin. The main pushback comes from the White House and GOP candidates rather than conservative outlets. Spokesman Davis Ingle said Democrats have no agenda to improve Americans' lives. Whatley didn't disavow the Camp Lejeune remarks, saying only that caring for affected veterans is a priority.

Watch for

Whether the remarks move suburban and veteran-heavy districts in North Carolina and Georgia. Whether any post-election aid decisions (Helene, Camp Lejeune, E15) track the results. That would likely bring Democratic oversight demands if they win the House.

Sources: AP via WSB-TV CNN NewsCord (coverage comparison)

Iran: Doha talks continue as Rubio says no strike decision yet and Khamenei orders forces to be ready

Facts

  • Iranian negotiators met Qatari mediators in Doha on Saturday, after more than 12 hours of talks in Tehran on Friday that a source told Reuters were coordinated with Washington. Tehran rejected Qatar's seven-day trust-building plan. Its own plan, which Trump has rejected, demands lifting the US blockade of Iranian ports, unfreezing assets and approving an Iranian-backed Hormuz route.
  • Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump hasn't decided on new strikes, prefers diplomacy, and that "talks have actually never stopped." Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Iran is studying a letter from VP JD Vance. Trump has downplayed the letter as being about medical supplies.
  • Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered the armed forces to prepare a "geographically unrestricted" response to any attack. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran is debating whether to lift its ban on nuclear weapons if fighting resumes, though no decision has been made.
  • Axios reports a US official saying Trump may "do something bold" if Republicans do badly Tuesday. A White House official denied that elections factor in. Per Axios, Hegseth and Rubio doubt a deal can be reached, while Vance, Witkoff and Kushner favor more talks.

Left view

International and left-leaning coverage (Al-Monitor/Reuters, Middle East Monitor relaying Axios) focuses on the electoral timing. Its argument: Washington is holding fire for domestic political reasons and using the threat of a post-election strike as leverage. That story also highlights Trump urging Israelis to keep Netanyahu in office so the two can "finish the job."

Right view

Little fresh right-leaning commentary surfaced today. The hawkish case is mostly coming from inside the administration. Per Axios, Hegseth and Rubio favor further weakening Iran's leadership over a deal. Rubio has previously said Trump won't allow "fake negotiations" to be used as a delay tactic.

Watch for

Allies were warned strikes could start as early as Nov. 4. With WTI above $100 and Brent well above that, analysts see any renewed strikes or Hormuz incidents pushing crude higher fast, which would undercut the winter-blend relief at the pump. Rezaei's nuclear-ban comment is the escalation tail risk to watch.

Sources: Reuters via Al-Monitor Axios via Middle East Monitor AP via Spectrum News Tribune India

Alaska Senate: DOJ asks a court to set aside every ballot cast for the "second Dan Sullivan"

Facts

  • The Justice Department wants all ballots for challenger Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. segregated. Its suit would delay certification if GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan loses and votes for the second Sullivan could have changed the result. The ballot lists both men, the incumbent with GOP and incumbent tags and the challenger with no party.
  • The New York Times reported that Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign worked with operatives to recruit the second Sullivan; the campaign denies it. A state judge restored his candidacy in June after the Division of Elections tried to disqualify him.
  • Peltola, the DSCC and the State of Alaska have all moved to dismiss. They argue the federal law DOJ cites covers voter registration, not ballot design. A federal judge has fast-tracked the case.

Left view

Democracy Docket and NBC News lead with the Democrats' filing, which calls DOJ's bid "wholly baseless." They cast the suit as a pre-planned way to block an Alaska result if the GOP loses.

Right view

Fox News leads with the "alleged spoiler plot" but concedes DOJ faces a "major legal hurdle." Heritage's Don Palmer says statistics alone won't prove confusion. Cato's Walter Olson thinks the state is likely to prevail, and Notre Dame's Derek Muller calls the needed analysis "impossible to measure after the fact."

Watch for

A ruling on the motions to dismiss could come before or right after Tuesday. Alaska's ranked-choice count runs for weeks, so if Senate control comes down to Alaska, this case could keep the chamber undecided into December.

Sources: CNBC Fox News Democracy Docket NBC News Alaska Public Media

Israel: thousands rally for an Eisenkot–Arab party deal to unseat Netanyahu

Facts

  • Final results leave Netanyahu's bloc with 53 of 120 Knesset seats and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc with 48, so neither can govern alone. Arab-led parties (Ra'am and the Joint List) won 19 seats on about 840,000 votes, a 64% jump from 2022.
  • Eisenkot had ruled out relying on Arab parties, but adding their 19 seats would give him 67. Thousands rallied in Tel Aviv urging him to make that deal, and Netanyahu supporters counter-protested.
  • Netanyahu accused Arab parties of "stealing" the election with Qatari money. Qatar called the charge disinformation.

Left view

Al Jazeera frames the record Arab turnout as the story of the election. It notes that right-wing circles have called the turnout "electoral terrorism," and treats the Tel Aviv rally as a "last chance for real change."

Right view

The Jerusalem Post's coverage focuses on Netanyahu's bloc leading in the count and on the coalition math. Likud and its allies argue a government relying on Arab parties would be illegitimate, a line amplified at the counter-protest.

Watch for

PBS NewsHour lays out the paths: a minority government, a unity deal, or a quick repeat election. The outcome shapes the Iran war. Trump has openly urged Israelis to keep Netanyahu, and an Eisenkot-led government could be more open to the Qatari track.

Sources: Al Jazeera Jerusalem Post PBS NewsHour

Ukraine: US clears a $2.1B sale of 500 Patriot missiles, but Zelensky warns delivery could take years

Facts

  • The State Department approved a potential $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 Patriot interceptors, with Lockheed Martin as prime contractor. Ukraine pays using money from Canada, Germany, Norway and other allies, and the department says no US funds are involved and US readiness won't suffer.
  • Zelensky thanked Trump but warned that delivery could take years. He asked the US and Europe to send Patriots from their own stockpiles now and refill them later from Ukraine's order. He says Russia has hit Ukraine's energy grid more than 30 times in two weeks.
  • The sale comes days after Trump waived new Russia sanctions just before they were set to take effect.

Left view

CNN stresses how scarce Patriot interceptors are and how long the production line is. It argues an approval that doesn't arrive before winter does little for Ukraine's grid right now, especially alongside the sanctions waiver.

Right view

No distinct right-leaning take surfaced today. Pro-administration framing emphasizes that Ukraine and Europe are paying and US taxpayers aren't. That's consistent with Trump's "they buy, we sell" approach to Kyiv.

Watch for

Whether European allies release stockpiled interceptors before peak winter strikes. More business for Lockheed's PAC-3 line, and pressure to expand production. Congressional pressure on the sanctions waiver if Democrats win the House.

Sources: CBS News CNN Kyiv Post Ukrainska Pravda

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,578.97, -1.8% Friday. Dow: 51,785.82, -1.1%. Nasdaq: 25,442.31, -2.8%, capping its worst month since March 2025. Intel (-29%, its worst day since 1974) and Reddit (-29%) led the tech rout (TheStreet).
  • Oil: WTI is holding just above $100 and Brent well above that heading into a week that could bring renewed US strikes on Iran. Any move on Hormuz is the swing factor.
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.18 per gallon (Oct. 31), down from $4.22 midweek and $4.41 on Oct. 1. AAA says triple-digit crude is limiting further declines even with winter-blend fuel.
  • Other: The 10-year Treasury yield is around 4.92% after a safety bid; bitcoin is near $77,000; gold is just under $4,000. This week: Election Day Tuesday, then the October jobs report.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Andrew Novak is running away with the VidantaWorld Mexico Open at 23-under through 54 holes, six clear of Matthieu Pavon (-17), with Doug Ghim third at -16. Final round today (PGA Tour).
  • Tennis: Basel upset: Valentin Vacherot beat No. 6 seed Taylor Fritz 7-6(5), 6-3 and plays Jiri Lehecka, who came from a set down against Jan-Lennard Struff, in today's final (ATP). The Paris Masters main draw is next.
  • Squash: No reliable PSA results retrieved today.
  • WWE: Crown Jewel is Saturday, Nov. 7 in Riyadh. The card: Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn and Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green for the Crown Jewel titles, Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton in Last Man Standing, and The Vision defending the tag titles against Penta and Je'Von Evans. item.title: Sat Oct 31, 2026 — Iran: Qatar races to broker talks as the US warns allies strikes could start Nov. 4
item.description: Iran: Qatar races to broker talks as the US warns allies strikes could start Nov. 4 · Wall Street's ugly October finale: Nasdaq sinks 2.9%, Intel has its worst day since 1974 · Midterms, 3 days out: record early vote, Democrats lead the generic ballot, Trump reverses on rallies · Alaska's "two Dan Sullivans" fight: NYT links Peltola's campaign, governor questions certification
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Iran: Qatar races to broker talks as the US warns allies strikes could start Nov. 4

Facts

  • Three Gulf Arab officials told MS NOW that Washington asked allies to prepare for a short, intense strike campaign on Iran beginning as early as Nov. 4, the day after the midterms. The White House doesn't comment on military planning; the US hasn't struck Iran since Sept. 1.
  • Qatari mediators spent more than 12 hours in Tehran Friday carrying a revised draft; CBS and a diplomatic source report "positive progress," and talks continue in Doha today. Iran had called the earlier draft "unacceptable" (Reuters via Middle East Eye).
  • The sticking points: Doha wants Iran to readmit UN inspectors in exchange for limited sanctions relief; Tehran wants the US naval blockade lifted, frozen funds released and oil sales allowed first. The WSJ reports CENTCOM's Adm. Brad Cooper briefed Trump in person on military options this week.
  • Inside the administration, Hegseth and Rubio reportedly doubt a deal is possible, while Vance, Witkoff and Kushner want talks. Saudi Arabia and Türkiye have urged Trump to give diplomacy more time.

Left view

Left-leaning and international outlets (Al Jazeera, Political Wire, Haaretz) focus on the timing: Trump promised no strikes before the vote, and a campaign queued for the day after reads to critics as war policy scheduled around an election. They highlight an Axios report that a US official said Trump could be more willing to strike if Republicans take heavy losses, a claim the White House rejects.

Right view

The hawkish case is being made mostly inside the administration rather than in op-eds this week: Hegseth and Rubio's camp argues Iran's current leadership won't give up enrichment, so pressure is the only leverage. Breitbart and other right-leaning outlets have covered the Qatari track largely straight. Note: I couldn't retrieve fresh National Review or Free Press pieces on this today.

Watch for

Whether Doha produces direct US-Iran talks before Tuesday. Tehran has threatened to hit oil and gas facilities in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain if the US targets its energy sector, and Iran's parliament has a bill to quit the NPT. Brent sits around $112-115; a renewed air campaign would likely push it higher and keep pump prices above $4.

Sources: Diplomatic Insight (MS NOW/Axios/CBS) Times of Israel Haaretz Middle East Eye Just Security (WSJ) Iran International Political Wire

Wall Street's ugly October finale: Nasdaq sinks 2.9%, Intel has its worst day since 1974

Facts

  • Friday's close: S&P 500 -1.8% to 7,580, Dow -1.1% to 51,770, Nasdaq -2.9% to 25,437. About 70% of US issues fell (TheStreet).
  • Intel dropped about 29% after a weak Q4 outlook citing a PC slump and a factory accident in Israel. Reddit also fell about 29% on soft guidance. Amazon's negative free cash flow added to fears over AI spending after Alphabet's record drop Thursday.
  • For October, the Nasdaq lost about 5.2%, its worst month since March 2025; the S&P fell about 1.2% while the Dow gained about 1.5% (Yahoo Finance). Bloomberg says the Nasdaq is nearing correction territory.

Left view

No distinctly left-leaning take retrieved; this is mostly a financial-press story. The skeptical line in mainstream coverage (CNN, Bloomberg) is that Big Tech is burning cash on data centers faster than revenue is coming in, and that index-fund savers are heavily exposed to a handful of companies.

Right view

Market-oriented voices are mostly calm. Truist's Keith Lerner called tech's roughly 10% slide normal for this bull market and said the long-term uptrend remains intact, seeing perhaps 2-8% more downside. Bloomberg reports traders are also pricing in AI-policy risk if Tuesday's midterms change control of Congress.

Watch for

Fed officials are talking up higher rates to fight inflation, and a December hike is increasingly expected (Yahoo Finance). With the 10-year yield near 4.93%, oil above $100 and the midterms Tuesday, analysts expect a volatile week; the VIX rose about 13% Friday.

Sources: Yahoo Finance TheStreet Bloomberg Bloomberg (AI policy) CNN

Midterms, 3 days out: record early vote, Democrats lead the generic ballot, Trump reverses on rallies

Facts

  • AP counted more than 43 million early or mail ballots five days out, about 10 million ahead of 2022; Texas is up 50% and Georgia has already passed its 2022 early total. Some trackers now put the figure near 48 million.
  • Democrats lead RealClearPolling's generic-ballot average 51.4%-43.2%. The PBS/NPR/Marist poll has them up 52-44 among likely voters, with Trump's approval at 40% and cost of living (34%) and democracy (33%) the top issues.
  • Trump reversed his cancellation and will rally Sunday in Kansas and Iowa, backing Sen. Roger Marshall (trailing Democrat Adam Hamilton 49-45 in an Emerson poll) and Ashley Hinson. At a Florida rally Friday he told supporters to act as if Republicans were behind.

Left view

NPR and PBS coverage stresses that "preserving democracy" ranks nearly level with prices, and that Trump disapproval is driving the early turnout. On PBS, Rahm Emanuel urged Democrats to treat a win as a "down payment" and present a concrete agenda, not just an anti-Trump vote.

Right view

The Washington Examiner has argued that a gerrymandered, sorted House map blunts any wave and that the Senate map still favors the GOP. Fox News's latest power rankings call the Senate a toss-up. Some Republicans are already looking ahead: Sen. Thom Tillis told PBS that Trump should "own" the outcome either way.

Watch for

Sabato's Kyle Kondik calls a House flip "almost certain" but the Senate "much more up in the air," with about seven toss-ups. Half of Republican likely voters plan to vote on Election Day versus 31% of Democrats, so expect early returns to look bluer before Election Day votes are counted.

Sources: Al Jazeera (AP) PBS/NPR/Marist PBS NewsHour Washington Examiner Newsweek Silver Bulletin

Alaska's "two Dan Sullivans" fight: NYT links Peltola's campaign, governor questions certification

Facts

  • The New York Times reported Wednesday that texts show Mary Peltola's (D) campaign discussed recruiting people named Dan Sullivan to confuse voters; retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan is now one of four names on the ranked-choice ballot against Sen. Dan Sullivan (R). Some sourcing comes from a former campaign manager, fired in August, who later tried to retract her comments.
  • Peltola's campaign says it had no involvement with either Sullivan campaign, and Dan J. Sullivan has denied running at Democrats' behest. The Alaska Supreme Court earlier ruled him eligible.
  • Gov. Mike Dunleavy (R) ordered an investigation and said certification "could be stopped" if Peltola wins. The Justice Department, which had already sued to halt certification of a possible Peltola win, issued new grand-jury subpoenas (Fox News, CNBC).

Left view

Alaska Public Media quoted legal experts who condemned the DOJ suit as an attempt to invalidate a vote before it happens, and Peltola and Democrats have moved to dismiss it. Axios and FAIR frame the governor's remarks as a threat to block a result Republicans don't like, saying the alleged tactic may be a dirty trick but isn't clearly illegal.

Right view

Fox News argues "legacy media" downplayed the scandal and focused on GOP reactions instead. Sen. Lisa Murkowski cited "a pattern of lies and coverups," and Trump called it "ELECTION FRAUD" and urged Peltola to drop out, without naming a specific crime.

Watch for

Notre Dame's Derek Muller called it a dirty campaign trick; experts told AP the report won't change the DOJ suit. If Peltola wins, The Hill expects a fight over seating her, and ranked-choice tabulation means the result could take days.

Sources: AP (via Fox13) Axios Fox News Alaska Public Media CNBC FAIR The Hill

Israel: Netanyahu loses his majority and his party calls the election "stolen"

Facts

  • After Tuesday's vote, Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's Jewish-led opposition 48, and Arab parties a record 19. Nobody reaches 61 without crossing lines most Zionist parties have ruled out (JTA, Times of Israel).
  • Likud says Arab parties "stole" the vote, citing allegations that Qatar secretly funded efforts to boost Arab turnout. The election committee chair asked the Shin Bet to investigate and report within a week; Qatar and Ra'am's Mansour Abbas deny any link.
  • Election officials say there's no basis for claims of systematic harm to the vote, and police say they have no evidence of fraud. President Herzog backed a thorough probe but warned against blaming Arab voters as a group.

Left view

Axios describes Netanyahu as trying to delegitimize results after losing his majority. Arab parties, quoted by the Times of Israel, call it a racist campaign; the group Standing Together has called rallies in five cities for a Jewish-Arab government.

Right view

Likud and its allies, amplified in Jerusalem Post coverage, argue that foreign money in Arab turnout drives is a real interference threat that has to be resolved before any coalition is built. They urge Zionist parties to refuse any deal relying on Ra'am or the Joint List.

Watch for

The Shin Bet report is due next week. Times of Israel analysis sees three paths: a repeat election, a weak Netanyahu caretaker government with no majority, or an unlikely Jewish-Arab coalition. CNBC expects weeks of coalition haggling.

Sources: JTA Times of Israel Axios Jerusalem Post Washington Post CNBC

Ukraine: Russian strike kills 14 on a Dnipro rail platform as Kyiv quietly halts refinery strikes

Facts

  • A Russian strike on a crowded railway platform in Dnipro killed at least 14 people; overnight attacks left more than 350,000 people in the area without power (Kyiv Post, Just Security).
  • The Wall Street Journal reports Ukraine has unofficially paused drone strikes on Russian oil refineries after weeks of Trump pressure over diesel prices before the midterms. Jared Kushner reportedly asked for a 30-day halt; Kyiv hasn't announced it.
  • Kyiv asked for something in return, either a Russian pause on energy strikes or more Patriot missiles, and got neither (Kyiv Post). Separately, a Melania Trump-brokered local ceasefire will let residents of Russian-held Oleshky get aid or leave.

Left view

Kyiv Post and other pro-Ukraine coverage frame it as Washington restraining Ukraine while Moscow keeps bombing. They argue Ukraine is giving up its most effective economic weapon for a US domestic political calendar.

Right view

The administration's case, as reported, is about prices: refinery strikes tighten global diesel supply while the Iran war already has crude above $100. Right-leaning outlets have given the pause little coverage; I couldn't retrieve a distinct conservative take today.

Watch for

The pause is expected to run past the midterms. Analysts say the Iran war, not Ukraine, is the main driver of fuel prices, so the diesel benefit may be small. Watch whether Kyiv resumes strikes after Tuesday and whether Zelensky gets the ballistic-missile defenses he says he needs.

Sources: Kyiv Post Just Security Global Banking & Finance (WSJ) PBS NewsHour

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,580, -1.8% Friday; -1.2% for October. Dow: 51,770, -1.1%; +1.5% for the month. Nasdaq: 25,437, -2.9%; about -5.2% for October, its worst month since March 2025. Russell 2000 -2.0%.
  • Oil: WTI December settled at $102.95 (+0.9%) on reports of post-midterm Iran strikes; Brent traded around $112-115. Exxon's Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B and Chevron's rose to $9.9B on war-driven prices.
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.20 per gallon Friday, down about 5 cents in a week and roughly 16 cents since early October; AAA says $100-plus crude is limiting further declines.
  • Other: 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.93% as investors sought safety; VIX about 19.4; gold -3.6%. Bitcoin is near $77,000 after the Binance hack. Fed speakers are leaning hawkish, and a December hike is increasingly priced in.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Andrew Novak tied the course record with a 10-under 61 to take a three-shot lead at 14-under at the VidantaWorld Mexico Open. Ben Griffin, Matthieu Pavon, Kihei Akina, Adrien Dumont de Chassart and Kensei Hirata are tied for second at -11 (PGA Tour).
  • Tennis: Basel semis today: Taylor Fritz vs. Valentin Vacherot. Fritz advanced when Arthur Fils retired with a back problem (6-2, 2-0), and Vacherot beat Holger Rune in three sets (ATP). The Paris Masters starts Monday.
  • Squash: No reliable PSA results retrieved today.
  • WWE: SmackDown: Sami Zayn kept the Undisputed WWE title over Trick Williams after the match was restarted as No DQ, winning with a low blow and a title shot. Chelsea Green retained against Nikki Bella with a roll-up. Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton is now Last Man Standing at Crown Jewel, Nov. 7 (WWE.com).
  • Hockey: Thursday: Canadiens won 5-2 in Dallas behind two goals each from Cole Caufield and Alex Newhook, their fourth straight win. Matthew Schaefer's second goal won it in OT for the Islanders over the Wild, and the Blues beat the Bruins (NHL.com).
  • Soccer: Premier League Halloween slate: Chelsea vs. Man Utd (8:30 a.m. ET), Man City vs. Brighton and Spurs vs. Palace. The big one is Sunday: Liverpool vs. Arsenal at Anfield (11:30 a.m. ET), a test of Arsenal's title credentials (SI).
  • Football: College today: No. 3 Georgia vs. No. 17 Florida in Atlanta (3:30 ET, ABC), No. 2 Ohio State at USC and No. 1 Miami vs. North Carolina (both 7:30 ET). NFL Sunday night: Eagles at Commanders (NBC).

item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Iran: Vance reaches out for talks while the US tells allies to brace for post-midterm strikes

Facts

  • Vice President Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing direct talks as soon as next week in Qatar or Turkey. The Wall Street Journal broke the story; the New York Times reports Qatari mediators delivered the letter Sunday.
  • Trump said he did not direct Vance to restart talks and described the outreach as being about medical supplies. He says he will choose between a deal and renewed major operations after the Nov. 3 midterms.
  • Per the WSJ, US officials told Gulf states to prepare for a brief but intense operation after the election; AP sources say allies expect Iranian retaliation against energy infrastructure. A Patriot battery, an extra carrier group and a Marine unit are moving to the region.
  • In Hormuz, a tanker was burning Thursday and the IRGC claimed three ships hit mines in a lane the US says it cleared. Reuters reports Iran called Qatar's latest draft deal unacceptable; CBS says Iran's formal answer is expected around Saturday.

Left view

Al Jazeera and other mainstream-left coverage frame the post-midterm timing as political: Trump ruled out new strikes before the vote, and critics argue a war decision is being held until after ballots are cast. The mixed signals between Vance and Trump are portrayed as an administration without a single Iran policy.

Right view

Hawkish voices on the right have been wary of Vance-led diplomacy since June, when Fox & Friends' Brian Kilmeade and Ben Shapiro called an earlier Iran memorandum "JD's deal" (per Media Matters' roundup). Newsmax framed this week's letter as Vance courting a hard-liner while Trump threatens force, a "peace through strength" pairing. I could not retrieve fresh National Review or Free Press pieces on the letter.

Watch for

Iran's reply to the Qatari draft (expected this weekend) and whether talks happen in Doha or Ankara next week. Rezaei warned Iran could hit US-linked infrastructure, including data centers. Any strike on Gulf energy would push Brent (already above $110) higher; the military has told Congress mine clearance in Hormuz could take months.

Sources: HNGN (WSJ/NYT/AP/Reuters roundup) Semafor Newsmax Al Jazeera Media Matters (June)

Big Tech earnings rout: Alphabet has its worst day ever, Intel and Amazon sink after hours

Facts

  • Alphabet closed down about 12.6% Thursday, its biggest one-day drop on record, after missing revenue and profit estimates, reporting slower search-ad growth and negative free cash flow (Finimize puts it at -$9.1B) on heavy AI spending.
  • After the bell, Intel fell about 23% on a weak fourth-quarter revenue forecast ($15-16B), and Amazon fell about 7% as trailing free cash flow turned deeply negative (about -$42B, per CNBC) despite strong AWS results.
  • Microsoft was the outlier: Azure grew 48% and its shares were roughly flat. The S&P 500 slipped 0.3% and the Nasdaq lost about 1.4%, though roughly 80% of S&P stocks actually rose (TheStreet). Nasdaq-100 futures were down about 2% overnight (CNBC).

Left view

No clearly left-leaning outlet retrieved; this is mostly a financial-press story. Skeptical coverage, such as The Motley Fool's "Is Wall Street ignoring the risk?" piece, focuses on hyperscalers burning cash to build data centers, with concentration risk for ordinary 401(k) holders when a handful of megacaps drive the index.

Right view

Market-oriented and business-right coverage (Conservative Daily News relaying the Amazon miss; Seeking Alpha contributors) frames it as investors disciplining capital spending, not an AI collapse. Some note Google Cloud demand suggests capex is, if anything, too small.

Watch for

Whether the selloff spreads at Friday's open. Asian markets already fell hard (reports say Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 5%). Analysts are watching Apple and Meta reactions, AI-related credit (data-center financing), and whether a narrow tech drawdown drags the whole index while yields sit above 5%.

Sources: TheStreet StockTitan CNBC CNBC (Amazon) Finimize Motley Fool Seeking Alpha

Binance hit by the largest crypto heist in history, about $6.3 billion

Facts

  • Binance says roughly $6.3B was stolen and about $3B has been frozen; it suspended all deposits and withdrawals and pledged to cover user losses (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, CNBC).
  • Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs attributes the attack with "high confidence" to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit, linked to the Lazarus Group. Early findings point to a compromised engineer's laptop.
  • The previous record was Lazarus's $1.5B Bybit theft in 2025. Bitcoin fell about 5%, below $77,000. Stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether froze affected funds (CNBC).

Left view

I could not retrieve a distinct left-leaning take today. The likely line of attack: the world's biggest exchange, which settled US money-laundering charges in 2023, still had a single-laptop point of failure, which could be used to argue for stricter custody rules. Tech press (TechCrunch) is covering it straight.

Right view

I could not retrieve a distinct right-leaning take today. Crypto-industry outlets (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph) emphasize the speed of freezes and Binance's reimbursement pledge as evidence the system is maturing; the national-security angle (North Korea funding weapons through theft) is the likeliest bipartisan thread.

Watch for

Withdrawals are expected to resume within about two days. Watch for a run on Binance once they do, US sanctions or Treasury action against laundering channels, and pressure on Congress's crypto market-structure push.

Sources: Al Jazeera Bloomberg CNBC TRM Labs TechCrunch CoinDesk

Midterms, 4 days out: Trump scraps Kansas and Iowa rallies; Fox calls the Senate a toss-up

Facts

  • Trump cancelled in-person rallies in Salina, Kansas (Saturday) and Dubuque, Iowa (Sunday), switching to telephone rallies across nearly 20 states. He said he doesn't feel he has to go to Kansas (Al Jazeera).
  • Fox News Power Rankings rate the Senate a toss-up, moving Ohio to Lean Democrat and South Carolina to toss-up. A Fox poll has Sherrod Brown (D) leading Sen. Jon Husted (R) 52-47 in Ohio.
  • New CNN polling: Talarico (D) 49, Paxton (R) 43 in Texas; El-Sayed (D) 49, Rogers (R) 42 in Michigan. RealClearPolling's generic ballot is D+8.2.
  • Alaska: DOJ issued more than 30 subpoenas over an alleged scheme to put a second "Dan Sullivan" on the ballot; Vance called for an investigation and Mary Peltola's campaign denies involvement (Fox).

Left view

Al Jazeera and CNN read the cancellations as a sign the GOP is playing defense on its own turf, pointing to Trump's 37% approval in Wisconsin's Marquette poll. NPR's race rankings now treat Texas and Ohio as genuinely competitive.

Right view

RNC Chair Joe Gruters says telephone rallies let Trump reach more voters. Fox highlights Husted defending the trade agenda (Ohio added 10,000 manufacturing jobs in 20 months, he says) and NRSC chair Tim Scott campaigning in Michigan, where a September Fox poll had the race within the margin.

Watch for

Prediction markets give Democrats very high odds for the House; the Senate likely comes down to Texas, Ohio, Alaska and Kansas. Alaska's result could be delayed by the ballot dispute. A Democratic House would open investigations and constrain Trump's agenda, including any Iran war authorization.

Sources: Al Jazeera Fox News NPR The Hill Washington Examiner (live)

ECB holds at 2.5% as Lagarde announces she will leave early, in February

Facts

  • The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% after two hikes this year, warning that rising energy prices pose upside inflation risks. Eurozone inflation was 3.8% in September, nearly double target (Euronews).
  • Christine Lagarde will step down Feb. 7, 2027, about nine months early. No reason was given; reports tie the timing to France's April 2027 presidential election. Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos and the Netherlands' Klaas Knot are seen as frontrunners.
  • French 10-year yields topped 5% last week for the first time since 2002 amid a budget standoff; Lagarde said the fix lies "at home in France."

Left view

European center-left coverage (Irish Times, RTÉ) emphasizes stability: the early exit lets the current French and German leaders shape the succession before a possible far-right win in France.

Right view

I did not retrieve a right-leaning outlet on this; coverage is mostly European and financial press. Bloomberg's framing is that the exit "compounds alarm" over oil and French debt.

Watch for

Succession jockeying among EU governments, French bond spreads (about 155 bp over Germany) and whether the ECB's never-used bond backstop comes into play. A weaker euro makes oil, priced in dollars, even costlier for Europe.

Sources: Euronews Bloomberg Irish Times RTÉ

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: -0.3% Thursday, snapping a three-day win streak. Dow: lower. Nasdaq: about -1.4%, dragged by Alphabet. Breadth was strong outside tech. Nasdaq-100 futures were down about 2% overnight after Intel and Amazon.
  • Oil: WTI about $102, Brent about $114 midday Thursday (TheStreet), easing slightly on Vance's diplomacy before Hormuz mine reports.
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.23 per gallon, down 5 cents in a week; AAA says $100-plus crude is limiting further declines.
  • Economy: Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualized (above 3.1% expected). September PCE inflation rose to 3.6% year over year, core 3.1%; real consumer spending was flat. The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% on Wednesday.
  • Crypto: Bitcoin below $77,000 after the Binance hack.

Sports Watercooler

  • Baseball (bonus): The Brewers won the first World Series in franchise history, beating the Rays 4-1 in Game 5 Wednesday to take the series 4-1. William Contreras was named MVP; Jacob Misiorowski threw 5⅔ scoreless innings (ESPN).
  • Golf: PGA Tour's VidantaWorld Mexico Open is under way in Nuevo Vallarta; Denny McCarthy, Austin Eckroat, Jeremy Paul and Sudarshan Yellamaraju shared the early lead at -3, with Max Homa and Ben Griffin a shot back (ESPN leaderboard, Round 1).
  • Tennis: Upset day in Basel: Swiss wild card Jerome Kym beat top seed Ben Shelton, and Jan-Lennard Struff knocked out Novak Djokovic in a third-set tiebreak. Arthur Fils and Taylor Fritz advanced (ATP). The Paris Masters main draw starts Monday.
  • Squash: No reliable PSA results retrieved today.
  • WWE: SmackDown tonight in Charleston: Sami Zayn defends the Undisputed WWE Championship against Trick Williams, and Chelsea Green defends the Women's title vs. Nikki Bella. Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton is set for Crown Jewel, Nov. 7 in Riyadh.
  • Hockey: Wednesday: Oilers blanked the Flames 4-0 and the Avalanche beat the Devils 5-2 (ESPN). Thursday results not retrieved.
  • Soccer: Premier League: Man City and Arsenal level on 21 points after eight games (City ahead on goal difference), with Brighton third on 16 and Liverpool fourth on 15 (NBC Sports).
  • Football: TNF: Packers 27, Panthers 19. Jordan Love threw for 288 yards and 3 TDs; Christian Watson had 113 receiving yards after returning from a chest-injury check; Green Bay sacked Bryce Young six times (Yahoo Sports).

The Big Stories Today

Midterms five days out: Democrats lead nationally, Senate map tightens in Texas, Ohio, Michigan

Facts

  • RealClearPolling's national average has Democrats up 51.4% to 43.2%; a Reuters/Ipsos poll (Oct 22-26) shows Democrats ahead by nine points among all voters, per Al Jazeera's roundup.
  • Republicans hold 53 Senate seats; Democrats need a net gain of four for control and a net three seats to flip the House.
  • Texas: Democrat James Talarico leads Republican Ken Paxton 48.5% to 46.7% in the RCP average. Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed (D) vs. Mike Rogers (R) ranges from a 2-point to a 7-point Democratic edge depending on the poll.
  • Trump campaigned in Ohio for Sen. Jon Husted (vs. Sherrod Brown); Obama was in Georgia for Sen. Jon Ossoff; Vance rallied in North Carolina for Michael Whatley (vs. Roy Cooper). Trump heads to South Carolina, Florida and Kansas through Saturday.

Left view

Al Jazeera and CNN stress a national environment favoring Democrats, with new polls described as good news for Senate hopes. Reuters/Ipsos finds 73% of adults think the cost of living is heading the wrong direction and Trump's approval at 32%.

Right view

Fox News columnist Hugh Hewitt argues Republicans must unite behind Paxton despite frustration with the nominee, warning that losing the Senate would open the door to impeachment efforts and sap Trump's remaining agenda. Fox News's own forecast moved Texas from Lean R to toss-up. Note: I could not retrieve fresh National Review or Washington Examiner pieces today, so right-leaning coverage here is thinner than usual.

Watch for

Al Jazeera's analysis notes Democrats could win North Carolina and Ohio and still fall short of 51 seats, so Texas, Alaska and Kansas may decide control. A House-only flip would let Democrats block parts of Trump's agenda and open investigations. Early Georgia voting ends Friday; rural-vs-metro turnout (21% vs. 24% in Texas) is the tell Republicans are watching.

Sources: Al Jazeera Al Jazeera (Oct 28) CNN Fox News Mediaite

Fed holds rates as Warsh vows not to "waver" on inflation; 10-year yield tops 5%

Facts

  • The Fed left rates unchanged Wednesday. CNN's headline says two officials dissented in favor of a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh emphasized bringing inflation down and said incoming data will guide the December meeting.
  • The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.02%, crossing 5% (Motley Fool). The S&P 500 closed up 0.28% near 7,744.
  • This is a hawkish-leaning Fed: at the July meeting three officials also dissented for a hike, with the policy rate at 3.50%-3.75% (AP via KSL).

Left view

I did not retrieve a distinct left-leaning take today. Mainstream coverage (CNN) leads with the unusual hawkish dissents; the cost-of-living angle is central to Democrats' midterm message.

Right view

No fresh right-leaning commentary retrieved. In July, the Washington Examiner framed the hold as expected given "too-high inflation" it tied partly to energy costs from the Iran war. Treat that as background, not today's framing.

Watch for

Analysts quoted in July (Inflation Insights' Omair Sharif) expected hikes unless the labor market weakened sharply; others (Nationwide's Kathy Bostjancic) argued rate hikes cannot fix an energy supply shock. With yields above 5%, mortgage and corporate borrowing costs stay elevated. December is the next decision point.

Sources: Motley Fool CNN AP via KSL (July) Washington Examiner (July)

Israel's election leaves no clear winner; Netanyahu bloc short of a majority

Facts

  • With about 86% of votes counted, Netanyahu's right-wing/religious bloc has 53 seats, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's bloc 48, and predominantly Arab parties 19. A government needs 61 (Ynet).
  • Likud has 26 seats, Eisenkot's Yashar! 21, Naftali Bennett's Beyachad 12, and the Arab Joint List 13. Late-counted military and double-envelope ballots could still shift seats.
  • Israel may stay under a caretaker government while coalition talks run; Netanyahu assured Ben Gvir and Smotrich he will not abandon them (Times of Israel).

Left view

Eisenkot said voters chose change and urged Netanyahu to step down; the Democrats' Yair Golan urged the opposition to build a government with Arab-party support, and Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen said his party is ready to help remove Netanyahu (Ynet).

Right view

Netanyahu called on Zionist parties to unite and thanked coalition partners. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Trump does not want Ben Gvir and likely Smotrich in the next government. I did not retrieve Israeli right-wing outlets' own framing today.

Watch for

Final counts and certification next week, then President's consultations on who gets first shot at forming a government. A stalemate raises the odds of a long caretaker period, which matters for Iran decisions: military action needs government or security cabinet approval.

Sources: Ynet Times of Israel

item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

DOJ charges Comey a third time, over a 2016 New York Times story

Facts

  • Prosecutors unsealed a two-count criminal information Monday accusing former FBI Director James Comey of transmitting, and conspiring to transmit, national defense information tied to an Oct. 5, 2016 New York Times article (Axios, Time).
  • The information was filed under seal Oct. 5. It skips a grand jury; the DOJ says it was filed to stop the statute of limitations from expiring while the investigation continues. Judge Trevor McFadden unsealed it but has not ruled on a motion to dismiss.
  • Two earlier cases: the false-statements indictment was dismissed in November 2025 over the prosecutor's appointment, and a case over the “86 47” post is set for trial in February 2027.
  • Separately Monday, a federal judge ruled that Comey's daughter Maurene, a former prosecutor, was unlawfully fired (Fox News).

Left view

Time and Axios stress that two prosecutor teams in Trump's first term declined to charge this same episode, that the filing appears to break the unofficial 60-day pre-election norm, and that Comey calls it persecution. The Times says such cases aim to chill sources.

Right view

Fox News presents it as the third matter against Comey and relays the DOJ position that filing an information to toll the statute of limitations is routine. Its coverage cited no Republican lawmakers; mainstream and right-leaning coverage of the legal merits was otherwise thin this morning.

Watch for

Whether McFadden accepts an information instead of an indictment; the limitations-period fight; whether prosecutors seek a grand jury before the Nov. 3 election. The statute-of-limitations dispute is the central legal question in the filings.

Sources: Axios Time Fox News

US forces reportedly ready to hit Iran within 96 hours of an order; decision expected after the midterms

Facts

  • CNN, citing two US officials, reports forces can launch a major operation within 96 hours of a presidential order; targets could include nuclear, military and energy sites. Trump has not decided, and officials say any order is more likely after Nov. 3.
  • Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials met Iranian leaders in Tehran, with Qatari mediation, to head off escalation in the eight-month war. Iran says it will reopen Hormuz if the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports; the US wants limits on enrichment.
  • Netanyahu reportedly asked for a joint strike before Israel's Oct. 27 election and Trump declined; his office denies this. The Houthis have attacked Saudi territory.
  • The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve is at its lowest level since 1982.

Left view

NPR's recent coverage emphasizes the economic fallout: jet fuel shortages, flight cuts and a nearly closed Hormuz. I did not retrieve a left-leaning take on the strike timing today.

Right view

Right-leaning framing, as in Fox News's Iran coverage, centers on Iranian attacks on shipping and mine-laying and on the blockade as leverage; Tehran's calls for a “single force” among Islamic nations get attention. I did not find a fresh right-leaning editorial on the strike timing today.

Watch for

Officials note Trump has appeared close to authorizing strikes before and backed off. Oil is the transmission channel: Brent is about $115 and WTI about $101, and Morgan Stanley is cited saying the fuel market stays tight through mid-2027.

Sources: Ynet / CNN report HNGN NPR Fox News

Midterms a week out: Democrats favored for the House, Senate in play

Facts

  • Election Day is Nov. 3. Democrats lead the generic ballot by about 9 points in Nate Silver's average and need a net three seats for the House (Yahoo News).
  • For the Senate, Democrats hold 47 seats and need four flips for 51. Polls show Democrats ahead in Maine, Ohio, North Carolina, Texas, Alaska and Michigan (D-held), with Iowa, Nebraska and Kansas close.
  • Trump's approval averages about 37% to 60% disapprove; on inflation and cost of living it is about 25% to 71%.
  • Redistricting in several Southern states may limit Democratic House gains.

Left view

The Yahoo News poll roundup frames it as Democratic momentum, with Trump's weak ratings on inflation and cost of living, and cautions that polls can be wrong. I did not retrieve a distinct left-leaning outlet take.

Right view

Fox News headlines say swing-state voters distrust the party they are backing and highlight Democratic criticism of Rep. Ilhan Omar days before the vote.

Watch for

Track the generic-ballot average and Senate toss-ups (Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas). Officials say any Iran strike order is more likely after Nov. 3.

Sources: Yahoo News Fox News

Anthropic files for a Nasdaq IPO, lifting tech stocks

Facts

  • Anthropic filed a prospectus with the SEC and plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. It had filed confidentially in June (TheStreet).
  • Earlier reports from the NYT and others put the target near a $2 trillion valuation and a raise above $100 billion; the prospectus terms were not confirmed in what I could read.
  • The news helped push the Nasdaq up 0.82% Monday as traders turned to a heavy big-tech earnings week.

Left view

I did not retrieve a left-leaning take on the filing today; coverage I saw was market-focused.

Right view

I did not retrieve a right-leaning take either; coverage was mostly market wires, so this story has no partisan split today.

Watch for

Pricing date and final valuation; whether Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon capex guidance this week supports the AI trade; supply effects of a very large listing on other tech stocks.

Sources: TheStreet Nasdaq.com

Fed meets today and tomorrow with inflation, not cuts, on the table

Facts

  • The FOMC meets Tuesday and Wednesday. Markets imply only about a 10% chance of a hike now, but traders watch Chair Kevin Warsh for signals on December (Capital.com via TheStreet).
  • Warsh has named October and December as decision points and signaled little tolerance for inflation above 2%.
  • The 10-year Treasury yield is about 4.98% and the 2-year about 4.71%.
  • Gas averages $4.29 a gallon, about 40% above a year ago.

Left view

No partisan commentary retrieved today; this is mainly a markets story.

Right view

No partisan commentary retrieved today; Warsh's own stated focus is holding inflation to 2%.

Watch for

A hold with hawkish language is the base case; a hike signal for December would pressure stocks and mortgage rates. Oil moves on Iran could change that math quickly.

Sources: TheStreet Kiplinger

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,676.80 (+0.70%). Dow: 52,361.52 (+0.28%). Nasdaq: 26,169.38 (+0.82%). Monday close, per TheStreet.
  • Oil: WTI fell 1.78% to $101.40 and Brent 1.34% to $115.20 on hopes of easing US-Iran tension; another report had Brent settling near $110.74.
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.2858, down about 20 cents from a month ago but up about $1.23 from a year ago.
  • Other: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report this week; 10-year yield about 4.98%.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Players keep leaving LIV, including Jon Rahm, Ian Poulter and Graeme McDowell, and Sergio Garcia has filed to end his contract; the DP World Tour reportedly plans a 2027 LIV ban (Golf Monthly). Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship.

The Big Stories Today

Iran standoff: Trump weighs a deal or force as Qatari mediators reach Tehran

Facts

  • Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran on Sunday in an effort coordinated with Washington, per an official cited by Discovery Alert; Trump is reportedly weighing a negotiated arrangement against further military action.
  • Fox News (Oct 25) reports intelligence warning that Iran may be stepping up efforts to target Americans. Details of the intelligence were not published in what I could access.
  • Oil dipped on the diplomacy: WTI was near $101 and Brent near $114 early Monday, after nearly reaching six-month highs last week.
  • Hormuz disruption remains the key variable for physical oil flows.

Left view

Mainstream and left-leaning outlets were not retrievable today (NYT, WaPo, Guardian, MSNBC, Vox were blocked or stale), so I can't attribute a left framing. Axios, a center outlet, frames the Iran dip as diplomacy-driven positioning rather than restored supply.

Right view

Fox News's weekend panel framed Trump's choice as "make a deal or finish them off," leaning on the intelligence warning about plots against Americans.

Watch for

Vanda Insights' Vandana Hari expects volatile, upside-skewed oil risks, with possible strikes on Iran not ruled out after the Nov 3 midterms. JPMorgan sees Brent averaging about $87 in 2027 if the conflict is prolonged versus about $64 in a peaceful baseline. Goldman has modelled about 21 days of very low Hormuz flows followed by a slow recovery.

Sources: Discovery Alert Fox News Axios

Trump's DOJ moves into the midterm homestretch: Alaska certification suit, raids and indictments

Facts

  • Oct 23: DOJ sued preemptively to block certification of Alaska's Senate result if GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola, arguing a second candidate with a similar name could confuse voters. Alaska's Supreme Court previously ruled that candidate belongs on the ballot.
  • Trump said he ordered the suit. DOJ also sued California over ballots from suspected noncitizens, and agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's home on Oct 12.
  • Virginia state Sen. Louise Lucas was indicted Oct 22 and two former senior FBI officials were charged Oct 23 with lying to Congress over the Hunter Biden probe (per Axios).
  • Democrats and voting-rights groups have moved to intervene and asked a judge to dismiss the Alaska case (NBC News, CNBC).

Left view

Peltola called the suit "desperate" and spoke of "corruption" (The Hill, MS NOW headlines); Democracy Docket and MS NOW cast it as a bid to rig the Senate race. Axios notes legal experts questioned DOJ's authority to block certification of a state-run election and that the timing breaks the pre-election norm of restraint.

Right view

Trump: "I'm the one that said, 'Do it.'" DOJ says an unlawful ballot, once counted, "cannot be uncounted," and calls links to the midterms a smear. AG Todd Blanche said the Lucas probe began under Biden and that he works for Trump. Trump separately blasted Alaska's ranked-choice voting as "corrupt" (Washington Examiner).

Watch for

Court rulings on the Alaska case before Nov 3 and any post-election certification fights. Control of the Senate (53-47 GOP) could hinge on these races; Democrats need a net four seats.

Sources: Axios NBC News CNBC The Hill Democracy Docket Washington Examiner

Michigan Senate race: Trump and Obama campaign, with nine days to the midterms

Facts

  • Trump rallied in Port Huron backing Mike Rogers (Senate) and John James (governor) and called Democrat Abdul El-Sayed a "jihadist"; El-Sayed's campaign rejected the claim.
  • Obama campaigned in Detroit for El-Sayed and gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson; Bernie Sanders rallied for El-Sayed in Grand Rapids.
  • Republicans hold the Senate 53-47 and the House 218-214; Democrats need a net four seats in each chamber.
  • Trump floated a $5,000 "Trump dividend" if Republicans win both chambers (per Fox live coverage).

Left view

Sanders called Trump "mentally unbalanced" and El-Sayed's campaign calls Rogers a "rubber stamp" for Trump (as relayed by Fox News's live blog). Obama framed his pitch around a Democratic Party that can tolerate disagreement (Washington Examiner headline).

Right view

Speaker Mike Johnson dismissed recent polls as "wrong," citing a CNN report that October polls undersampled Republicans; Scalise called it a turnout contest. Notably, Rogers broke with Trump: "I've never called him a terrorist" (Washington Examiner).

Watch for

Turnout in Michigan and the Senate map decide chamber control. Analysts cited by Reuters (via Fox) lay out split-chamber outcomes as plausible.

Sources: Fox News live blog Washington Examiner Washington Examiner

Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil

Facts

  • Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff Sunday over Flavio Bolsonaro, son of Jair Bolsonaro, according to early results (Axios). The margin was not reported in what I could access.
  • Flavio Bolsonaro said he would not accept the result and called for it to be annulled, per translations cited by Axios.
  • The U.S. had imposed additional 25% tariffs on some Brazilian goods; Lula called Flavio "Trump's candidate" during the campaign.

Left view

Left-leaning outlets weren't retrievable today. Axios (center) characterizes the result as a setback for the right-wing populist movement and a counterweight to Trump's influence in Latin America.

Right view

Fox News led with "conservative wave hits roadblock," framing Lula as holding off the Bolsonaro challenge. No direct Trump reaction was reported in the sources I reached.

Watch for

Tariff tensions likely persist. Watch whether Flavio Bolsonaro's refusal to concede turns into protests or court challenges.

Sources: Axios Fox News

Israel votes Tuesday with Netanyahu's coalition trailing in final polls

Facts

  • Final polls from three major Israeli networks put Netanyahu's bloc near 50 of 120 seats, 17 fewer than his current coalition; Likud at about 20 versus 32 now.
  • Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc is projected at 52-56 seats; Arab parties at 14-16 combined. Pro-Netanyahu Channel 14 is the outlier, giving his bloc 60.
  • Netanyahu spoke with Trump twice in three days seeking more public backing, per Axios sources; Likud denied it. A U.S. official called it a "sign of desperation."

Left view

Mainstream and left outlets not retrievable today for attribution.

Right view

Fox News is running an Israeli surprise-attack drill story with an expert invoking 1973. Right-leaning framing of Netanyahu's request was not available beyond Likud's denial.

Watch for

A hung result could mean weeks of coalition talks, which matters for Iran policy and Gaza ceasefire arrangements. Watch for further Trump statements on the election.

Facts

Fox and the Washington Examiner both lead with Machado's return; the Examiner stresses lingering doubts about Venezuelan democracy.
